name: scan0050-text-0204
text: THE ALTITUDE CONTROL.

name: scan0050-text-0205
text: The official Zenith jets for the Liberty engine are :—

name: scan0050-text-0206
text: The density of the air decreases rapidly within the

name: scan0050-text-0207
text: altitudes now reached by aeroplanes. The deficiency of

name: scan0050-text-0208
text: oxygen then results in an over rich mixture, which is

name: scan0050-text-0209
text: corrected by reducing the flow of petrol in proportion to

name: scan0050-text-0210
text: altitude. This correction is effected by the pilot at his

name: scan0050-text-0211
text: discretion by means of a separate control lever. On the

name: scan0050-text-0212
text: carburettor under notice the “vacuum” system is em-

name: scan0050-text-0213
text: ployed. The flow of petrol from the float chamber to

name: scan0050-text-0214
text: the main jet depends upon a difference between the

name: scan0050-text-0215
text: pressure ruling in the float and mixing chambers respec-

name: scan0050-text-0216
text: tively. Whereas the float chamber is subject to atmos-

name: scan0050-text-0217
text: pheric pressure, the mixing chamber is governed by a

name: scan0050-text-0218
text: “depression,” which may alternatively be described as

name: scan0050-text-0219
text: a partial vacuum, due to the descent of the pistons in the

name: scan0050-text-0220
text: cylinders of the engine. Thus, if the petrol in the car-

name: scan0050-text-0221
text: burettor be regarded as a U-shaped column, there is

name: scan0050-text-0222
text: atmospheric pressure at the float chamber tip of the U,

name: scan0050-text-0223
text: and a depression at the mixing chamber tip of the U.

name: scan0050-text-0224
text: The flow of petrol depends upon the difference between

name: scan0050-text-0225
text: these two pressures. It is thus a simple matter to cut

name: scan0050-text-0226
text: down the supply of petrol at high altitudes by reducing

name: scan0050-text-0227
text: the pressure in the float chamber. Under the vacuum

name: scan0050-text-0228
text: system of altitude control, the float chamber is fitted

name: scan0050-text-0229
text: with an airtight lid, and is supplied with air at ground

name: scan0050-text-0230
text: level and at moderate altitudes through a small hole

name: scan0050-text-0231
text: communicating with the atmosphere and termed a “leak

name: scan0050-text-0232
text: hole.” So long as the leak hole alone is in action,

name: scan0050-text-0233
text: atmospheric pressure governs the float chamber, and the

name: scan0050-text-0234
text: maximum supply of petrol is assured. As the aeroplane

name: scan0050-text-0235
text: gains altitude, and the petrol supply becomes excessive, the

name: scan0050-text-0236
text: control cock is operated to connect up a “suction hole”

name: scan0050-text-0237
text: with the float chamber. This suction hole draws air

name: scan0050-text-0238
text: to the depression area at the narrowest diameter of

name: scan0050-text-0239
text: the choke tube: the pressure in the float chamber is

name: scan0050-text-0240
text: proportionately reduced, and the petrol supply is cut

name: scan0050-text-0241
text: down.

name: scan0050-text-0242
text: The details of the control on this type of Zenith

name: scan0050-text-0243
text: carburettor have been modified for the British Services,

name: scan0050-text-0244
text: and are shown in Figs. 38 and 42. The bridge piece

name: scan0050-text-0245
text: between the choke tubes contains a hollow chamber,

name: scan0050-text-0246
text: connected as follows:—

name: scan0050-text-0247
text: Choke Tube

name: scan0050-text-0248
text: 36 mm.

name: scan0050-text-0249
text: Main Jet

name: scan0050-text-0251
text: Compensator

name: scan0050-text-0253
text: Shroud Tube

name: scan0050-text-0254
text: 3.9 mm. diameter.

name: scan0051-text-0256
text: Claudel-Hobson Carburettor,

name: scan0051-text-0257
text: Type H.C. 7.

name: scan0051-text-0258
text: i. By the hole P to the float chamber.

name: scan0051-text-0259
text: ii. By the pipe O to the main air intake. This

name: scan0051-text-0260
text: pipe O is the “leakhole.”

name: scan0051-text-0261
text: iii. By the duct Q to the housing of the altitude

name: scan0051-text-0262
text: control cock, from which the “suction holes”

name: scan0051-text-0263
text: R open into the mixing chamber.

name: scan0051-text-0264
text: The pipe or leakhole O is permanently open. So long

name: scan0051-text-0265
text: as the suction holes R are closed by the altitude control

name: scan0051-text-0266
text: cock, O forms the sole air supply to the float chamber,

name: scan0051-text-0267
text: and the flow of petrol to the main jet is at its maximum.

name: scan0051-text-0268
text: As the control cock is progressively operated to open up

name: scan0051-text-0269
text: the suction holes R, the pressure in the float chamber

name: scan0051-text-0270
text: is weakened, and the flow of petrol to the jet is reduced.

name: scan0051-text-0271
text: This carburettor aims at providing a predetermined

name: scan0051-text-0272
text: petrol-air ratio over the full range of engine speeds by a

name: scan0051-text-0273
text: principle quite different to that employed in the Zenith.

name: scan0051-text-0274
text: In outline the system is as follows:—

name: scan0051-text-0275
text: (a) Throttle shut to slow-running position. The

name: scan0051-text-0276
text: petrol supply is restricted by a calibrated

name: scan0051-text-0277
text: pilot jet: the air supply is automatically

name: scan0051-text-0278
text: Fig. 42.

name: scan0051-text-0279
text: Diagram illustrating Zenith Altitude Control.

name: scan0051-text-0280
text: O—Leakhole.

name: scan0051-text-0281
text: P—Lead to float chamber.

name: scan0051-text-0282
text: R—Suction hole.

name: scan0052-text-0284
text: restricted by the slow speed of the engine:

name: scan0052-text-0285
text: indeed, the velocity of the air would be too

name: scan0052-text-0286
text: low to pick up petrol if the air were not

name: scan0052-text-0287
text: drawn through narrow passages, e.g., a

name: scan0052-text-0288
text: strangling slot in the throttle barrel, and a

name: scan0052-text-0289
text: small bore by-pass: these narrow passages

name: scan0052-text-0290
text: increase the velocity of the air stream.

name: scan0052-text-0291
text: (b) Full throttle opening. The petrol supply is

name: scan0052-text-0292
text: determined by a calibrated main jet of the

name: scan0052-text-0293
text: submerged type, mounted at the base of a

name: scan0052-text-0294
text: “diffuser” in the mixing chamber. The

name: scan0052-text-0295
text: volume and velocity of the air stream are

name: scan0052-text-0296
text: conditioned by the diameter of the choke

name: scan0052-text-0297
text: tube, etc.

name: scan0052-text-0298
text: Fig. 43.

name: scan0052-text-0299
text: H.C. 7 Duplex Carburettor.

name: scan0053-text-0301
text: (c) Intermediate throttle openings. As ex-

name: scan0053-text-0302
text: plained on page 43, the tendency of a crude

name: scan0053-text-0303
text: carburettor is to supply an excess of petrol

name: scan0053-text-0304
text: when the depression or suction reaches a

name: scan0053-text-0305
text: maximum at high engine speeds. This ten-

name: scan0053-text-0306
text: dency is counteracted in the H.C. 7 by the

name: scan0053-text-0307
text: calibrated main jet; its maximum delivery

name: scan0053-text-0308
text: is correct for high engine speeds. Such a

name: scan0053-text-0309
text: system introduces a fresh difficulty. If the

name: scan0053-text-0310
text: petrol supply is correct at full speed, it is

name: scan0053-text-0311
text: likely to be deficient at quarter, half, and

name: scan0053-text-0312
text: three-quarter throttle openings, when the

name: scan0053-text-0313
text: depression is less. This difficulty is over-

name: scan0053-text-0314
text: come by employing a varying petrol level

name: scan0053-text-0315
text: in the diffuser tube. At intermediate

name: scan0053-text-0316
text: speeds the main jet passes slightly more

name: scan0053-text-0317
text: petrol than can be atomised. This small

name: scan0053-text-0318
text: surplus of spirit forms a reserve in the

name: scan0053-text-0319
text: diffuser, and the amount of the reserve will

name: scan0053-text-0320
text: vary in proportion to the engine speed. As

name: scan0053-text-0321
text: the diffuser is formed from tubes of small

name: scan0053-text-0322
text: diameter, the level of the petrol in the

name: scan0053-text-0323
text: diffuser will also vary. As the level falls,

name: scan0053-text-0324
text: the main jet is progressively relieved of

name: scan0053-text-0325
text: suction by air entering through the holes

name: scan0053-text-0326
text: in the diffuser tube.

name: scan0053-text-0327
text: Consequently, as the engine is acceler-

name: scan0053-text-0328
text: ated from its minimum towards its maxi-

name: scan0053-text-0329
text: mum speed, the petrol level is gradually

name: scan0053-text-0330
text: and automatically lowered by the depletion

name: scan0053-text-0331
text: of the reserve in the diffuser tubes; and,

name: scan0053-text-0332
text: contrariwise, as the engine is slowed down,

name: scan0053-text-0333
text: the reserve is built up again, and the level

name: scan0053-text-0334
text: rises. Thus the tendency of an increasing

name: scan0053-text-0335
text: depression to enrich the mixture is counter-

name: scan0053-text-0336
text: acted, and vice versâ.

name: scan0053-text-0337
text: The diffuser tube also serves a further purpose.

name: scan0053-text-0338
text: In carburettors fitted with a simple jet, a stream of pure

name: scan0053-text-0339
text: petrol issues from the top of the jet, and is not mixed

name: scan0053-text-0340
text: with air until it enters the choke tube. With a diffuser

name: scan0053-text-0341
text: type of jet, a small quantity of air is drawn at high

name: scan0053-text-0342
text: velocity through the jet, and is mixed with the petrol

name: scan0053-text-0343
text: before the latter issues into the choke tube. (The quan-

name: scan0053-text-0344
text: tity of air depends upon the number of air holes in the

name: scan0053-text-0345
text: diffuser tube uncovered by the falling petrol level.) Thus,

name: scan0053-text-0346
text: instead of delivering pure petrol, the diffuser sprays out

name: scan0053-text-0347
text: an “emulsion” of mingled petrol vapour and air into

name: scan0053-text-0348
text: the stream of air drawn up from the main intake. This

name: scan0053-text-0349
text: emulsion impinges into the main air stream at high speed,

name: scan0054-text-0351
text: and at a sharp angle; atomisation is consequently

name: scan0054-text-0352
text: thorough.

name: scan0054-text-0353
text: The sectional drawing, Fig. 44, and the photograph,

name: scan0054-text-0354
text: Fig. 43, illustrate the construction of the carburettor,

name: scan0054-text-0355
text: and its appearance. The throttle is shown in Fig. 45;

name: scan0054-text-0356
text: the slot in the barrel closes round the top of the slow-

name: scan0054-text-0357
text: running position when the throttle is closed, and acts

name: scan0054-text-0358
text: as an air strangler, concentrating the depression round

name: scan0054-text-0359
text: the head of the tube. The slow-running mixture is drawn

name: scan0054-text-0360
text: into the engine partly via the by-pass shown in Fig. 44,

name: scan0054-text-0361
text: and partly through the V in the back of the throttle.

name: scan0054-text-0362
text: Fig. 44.

name: scan0054-text-0363
text: Section of H.C. 7 Carburettor.

name: scan0054-text-0364
text: Fig. 45.

name: scan0054-text-0365
text: The H.C. 7 Throttle Barrel.

name: scan0055-text-0367
text: The diffuser is illustrated in Figs. 46, 47. Petrol

name: scan0055-text-0368
text: passes through the main jet A into the base of the diffu-

name: scan0055-text-0369
text: ser: the main jet A determines the rate of the

name: scan0055-text-0370
text: petrol supply, and its effective diameter must on

name: scan0055-text-0371
text: no account be tampered with, e.g., by cleaning

name: scan0055-text-0372
text: with a broach. The petrol then fills the three concentric

name: scan0055-text-0373
text: tubes B, N and M to a maximum height, determined

name: scan0055-text-0374
text: by the adjustment of the float needle. This maximum

name: scan0055-text-0375
text: height will be set at 8 mm. below the lip of the “guard”

name: scan0055-text-0376
text: tube M; other considerations, as is explained below,

name: scan0055-text-0377
text: affect the level while the engine is running. The action

name: scan0055-text-0378
text: of these tubes will now be described in detail.

name: scan0055-text-0379
text: The Slow-Running Tube B.—The slow-running tube

name: scan0055-text-0380
text: B is mounted in series with the main jet A, i.e., it

name: scan0055-text-0381
text: receives its petrol supply via A and D, instead of through

name: scan0055-text-0382
text: a separate duct: the method of supply makes for fuel

name: scan0055-text-0383
text: economy, as B tends to go out of action when the

name: scan0055-text-0384
text: throttle is opened. A constriction in the inner diameter

name: scan0055-text-0385
text: of B at the point X forms the pilot jet. There are two

name: scan0055-text-0386
text: separate air supplies for slow-running purposes. Air

name: scan0055-text-0387
text: from the main intake enters the “air” tube P through

name: scan0055-text-0388
text: the holes H, passes up P, over the lip of the “guard” tube

name: scan0055-text-0389
text: Fig. 46.

name: scan0055-text-0390
text: Section of the H.C. 7 Diffuser.

name: scan0056-text-0392
text: M, and through the depression holes F F into the

name: scan0056-text-0393
text: “diffuser” tube N. From N the air passes into the slow-

name: scan0056-text-0394
text: running tube B via the holes E E, immediately above the

name: scan0056-text-0395
text: pilot jet X. This air is mixed with petrol before it

name: scan0056-text-0396
text: emerges from the head of tube B. A second air supply

name: scan0056-text-0397
text: is drawn up through the main air intake, its velocity being

name: scan0056-text-0398
text: greatly increased by the strangler slot in the throttle

name: scan0056-text-0399
text: barrel, which slides down round the top of B in the closed

name: scan0056-text-0400
text: position of the throttle. The slow-running mixture

name: scan0056-text-0401
text: passes towards the engine through the by-pass shown in

name: scan0056-text-0402
text: Fig. 44, which is adjustable by means of a screw.

name: scan0056-text-0403
text: The main jet A passes more petrol than can be

name: scan0056-text-0404
text: atomised through the tube B. Consequently, while the

name: scan0056-text-0405
text: engine is running slowly, the tubes N and M fill up with

name: scan0056-text-0406
text: petrol to the fixed maximum level, in readiness for the

name: scan0056-text-0407
text: liberal supply of petrol required for acceleration.

name: scan0056-text-0408
text: The Depression Tube N.—On the throttle being

name: scan0056-text-0409
text: opened, the depression immediately begins to act upon

name: scan0056-text-0410
text: the depression tube N through the emulsion holes G G.

name: scan0056-text-0411
text: Petrol is drawn out through G G, and is already mixed

name: scan0056-text-0412
text: with air drawn through the diffuser holes F F, over the

name: scan0056-text-0413
text: lip of the guard tube M, out of the air tube P. This air

name: scan0056-text-0414
text: and petrol are already mixed together when they emerge

name: scan0056-text-0415
text: from G G, and impinge upon the stream of air drawn

name: scan0056-text-0416
text: up outside the diffuser from the main intake.

name: scan0056-text-0417
text: Fig. 47.

name: scan0056-text-0418
text: Parts of the Diffuser (shown dismantled).

name: scan0057-text-0420
text: As the engine speed rises there would be a tendency

name: scan0057-text-0421
text: for an excessive amount of petrol to be atomised, if the

name: scan0057-text-0422
text: level in the diffuser remained constant. But the main

name: scan0057-text-0423
text: jet A is not large enough to maintain the maximum level

name: scan0057-text-0424
text: of petrol in the tubes M, N, and B permanently; so the

name: scan0057-text-0425
text: mixture remains constant.

name: scan0057-text-0426
text: If the engine is throttled right down again, the slow-

name: scan0057-text-0427
text: running tube B comes into action afresh, and a reserve

name: scan0057-text-0428
text: of petrol again accumulates in M and N.

name: scan0057-text-0429
text: The guard tube M is obviously provided to retain

name: scan0057-text-0430
text: petrol in the depression tube N, whilst allowing air to

name: scan0057-text-0431
text: enter N at the holes F F: it is essential that some of the

name: scan0057-text-0432
text: holes F F shall be near the surface of the petrol at all

name: scan0057-text-0433
text: its varying levels, so that they are drilled at intervals

name: scan0057-text-0434
text: from the bottom to the top.

name: scan0057-text-0435
text: The air tube P increases the velocity of the air which

name: scan0057-text-0436
text: is drawn through the diffuser.

name: scan0057-text-0437
text: (Readers familiar with the earlier issues of the H.C. 7

name: scan0057-text-0438
text: type should note that no air cones are now fitted round

name: scan0057-text-0439
text: the diffuser.)

name: scan0057-text-0440
text: Adjustments.—No adjustments to the diffuser assem-

name: scan0057-text-0441
text: bly are possible or desirable, as its working depends

name: scan0057-text-0442
text: upon a variety of orifices, all of which are calibrated.

name: scan0057-text-0443
text: Nor must any attempt be made to dismantle the unit

name: scan0057-text-0444
text: consisting of tubes N, M and P. The tube N is expanded

name: scan0057-text-0445
text: into position, and the parts are soldered together: any

name: scan0057-text-0446
text: tampering will merely result in wrecking the assembly.

name: scan0057-text-0447
text: Cleaning should be done by blowing through, and not

name: scan0057-text-0448
text: with broaches. The sole permissible adjustment which

name: scan0057-text-0449
text: affects the diffuser, is the setting of the petrol level,

name: scan0057-text-0450
text: which should be kept at 8 mm. below the lip of the tube

name: scan0057-text-0451
text: M: the collar is a tapping fit on the float needle, to

name: scan0057-text-0452
text: which it is lightly soldered after setting.

name: scan0057-text-0453
text: The slow-running mixture can be adjusted for quan-

name: scan0057-text-0454
text: tity by setting the adjusting screw of the by-pass

name: scan0057-text-0455
text: (Fig. 44); and for quality, by setting the adjustable

name: scan0057-text-0456
text: throttle stop screw. It might appear that the latter

name: scan0057-text-0457
text: would only affect the quantity of the mixture; but it

name: scan0057-text-0458
text: governs the strangling effect of the throttle slot round

name: scan0057-text-0459
text: the head of tube B, and so varies the quality.

name: scan0057-text-0460
text: These adjustments will usually repay trouble after

name: scan0057-text-0461
text: an engine has been overhauled, as the sum total of the

name: scan0057-text-0462
text: air leaks at the various joints in the induction system

name: scan0057-text-0463
text: must inevitably vary. The adjustment should be made

name: scan0057-text-0464
text: with the engine warm, as its purpose is not so much to

name: scan0057-text-0465
text: secure the best starting adjustment, as to obtain an

name: scan0057-text-0466
text: economical setting on which an engine can be trusted

name: scan0057-text-0467
text: not to choke when throttled down during flight. The

name: scan0057-text-0468
text: procedure is therefore as follows:—

name: scan0058-text-0470
text: FITTING NOTES.

name: scan0058-text-0471
text: i. Warm up the engine.

name: scan0058-text-0472
text: ii. Set the throttle stop, till the engine just keeps

name: scan0058-text-0473
text: running, and no more.

name: scan0058-text-0474
text: iii. Unscrew the by-pass adjustment a little, so

name: scan0058-text-0475
text: that the engine runs a shade faster.

name: scan0058-text-0476
text: iv. Slow the engine down a little by resetting the

name: scan0058-text-0477
text: throttle stop.

name: scan0058-text-0478
text: By the above method, the desired minimum engine

name: scan0058-text-0479
text: speed is attained, plus a little extra strangling of the air,

name: scan0058-text-0480
text: which will facilitate starting.

name: scan0058-text-0481
text: The standard Claudel jet sizes for the Liberty engine

name: scan0058-text-0482
text: are:—

name: scan0058-text-0483
text: If a light carburettor is bolted up to an untrue

name: scan0058-text-0484
text: induction pipe flange, the carburettor body may be dis-

name: scan0058-text-0485
text: torted, and the throttle will bind. It is therefore

name: scan0058-text-0486
text: essential to ensure a true jointing face on the induction

name: scan0058-text-0487
text: manifold. This is peculiarly difficult with the Liberty

name: scan0058-text-0488
text: engine, on which one carburettor face beds against ports

name: scan0058-text-0489
text: in two separate induction manifolds: and the need for

name: scan0058-text-0490
text: extreme care in erecting the cylinders and their mani-

name: scan0058-text-0491
text: folds is indicated.

name: scan0058-text-0492
text: Thin fibre washers are exclusively used for jointing,

name: scan0058-text-0493
text: except at the joint between the two halves of the car-

name: scan0058-text-0494
text: burettor, where a thin (.01 in. maximum) paper washer is

name: scan0058-text-0495
text: employed.

name: scan0058-text-0496
text: The main jet must make a petrol tight joint with its

name: scan0058-text-0497
text: seating, or the calibration of the jet becomes futile.

name: scan0058-text-0498
text: The movement of the altitude control lever is short,

name: scan0058-text-0499
text: owing to the limited travel of the small cock; the

name: scan0058-text-0500
text: leverage should therefore be multiplied in linking this

name: scan0058-text-0501
text: lever to the cock it controls.

name: scan0058-text-0502
text: Care must be taken to synchronise the controls, so

name: scan0058-text-0503
text: that movements of the cockpit levers affect both car-

name: scan0058-text-0504
text: burettors identically: this, of course, applies to the alti-

name: scan0058-text-0505
text: tude controls as well as to the throttles. Spare vacuum

name: scan0058-text-0506
text: cocks are interchangeable, in the event of wear or

name: scan0058-text-0507
text: damage. Under no circumstances must the holes or

name: scan0058-text-0508
text: slots be tampered with in squadrons.

name: scan0058-text-0509
text: If the petrol is pressure-fed, the relief valve must

name: scan0058-text-0510
text: act at 3 lbs. per square inch (absolute maximum). If

name: scan0058-text-0511
text: fuel is fed by gravity, the head must not be less than

name: scan0058-text-0512
text: two feet.

name: scan0058-text-0513
text: Main

name: scan0058-text-0515
text: Pilot

name: scan0059-text-0518
text: POSSIBLE CAUSES OF TROUBLE.

name: scan0059-text-0519
text: THE ALTITUDE CONTROL.

name: scan0059-text-0520
text: I. Absence or Shortage of Petrol.

name: scan0059-text-0521
text: 1. Choked jets. Clear by blowing; the use of

name: scan0059-text-0522
text: broaches is forbidden.

name: scan0059-text-0523
text: 2. Dirt in tanks, supply piping, or filter.

name: scan0059-text-0524
text: 3. Air lock in supply piping.

name: scan0059-text-0525
text: 4. Needle valve stuck.

name: scan0059-text-0526
text: 5. Toggle levers jambed.

name: scan0059-text-0527
text: 6. Empty tanks.

name: scan0059-text-0528
text: 7. Excessive heat, producing vapour lock in

name: scan0059-text-0529
text: supply pipe.

name: scan0059-text-0530
text: II. Excess of Petrol: “Flooding.”

name: scan0059-text-0531
text: 1. Damaged, bent, worn, or eccentric needle.

name: scan0059-text-0532
text: 2. Faulty needle seating (removable without dis-

name: scan0059-text-0533
text: mantling carburettor).

name: scan0059-text-0534
text: 3. Damaged washers on jet or needle seatings.

name: scan0059-text-0535
text: 4. Other forms of leak at main jet seating.

name: scan0059-text-0536
text: 5. Petrol level too high.

name: scan0059-text-0537
text: 6. Toggle levers jambed.

name: scan0059-text-0538
text: 7. Excessive pressure in tank.

name: scan0059-text-0539
text: 8. Punctured float.

name: scan0059-text-0540
text: III. Defective Altitude Control.—When this is in

name: scan0059-text-0541
text: order, opening the cocks fully should reduce the engine

name: scan0059-text-0542
text: speed from 1,400 r.p.m. to about 1,200 r.p.m. at ground

name: scan0059-text-0543
text: level. Needless to say, this test should only be made

name: scan0059-text-0544
text: with the machine chocked and stationary, and the test

name: scan0059-text-0545
text: should be barely long enough for the tachometer needle

name: scan0059-text-0546
text: to record the drop. Such a test will not be made in

name: scan0059-text-0547
text: flight; and if the altitude control should be held open

name: scan0059-text-0548
text: for more than a few seconds in a ground level test, the

name: scan0059-text-0549
text: engine might catch fire.

name: scan0059-text-0550
text: No trouble can arise with the altitude control ex-

name: scan0059-text-0551
text: cept as the result of wear, dirt, careless adjustment of

name: scan0059-text-0552
text: the control linkage, or unwarranted interferences with

name: scan0059-text-0553
text: the parts.

name: scan0059-text-0554
text: As explained on p. 48, a carburettor setting which

name: scan0059-text-0555
text: is correct at ground level will be far too rich at altitude

name: scan0059-text-0556
text: unless special precautions are taken. The vacuum sys-

name: scan0059-text-0557
text: tem is adopted in the H.C. 7 carburettor.

name: scan0059-text-0558
text: The petrol supply from the float to the jet depends

name: scan0059-text-0559
text: on differences of pressure, as explained on page 48. The

name: scan0059-text-0560
text: rate of supply can thus be slowed down by reducing the

name: scan0059-text-0561
text: pressure in the float chamber. This is easily arranged.

name: scan0059-text-0562
text: The cover of the float chamber is provided with an air-

name: scan0059-text-0563
text: tight joint, and air is supplied to the float chamber

name: scan0059-text-0564
text: through a permanent “leak hole” of small diameter,

name: scan0060-text-0566
text: THE USE OF THE VACUUM CONTROL.

name: scan0060-text-0567
text: opening into the atmosphere. In addition, the air space

name: scan0060-text-0568
text: in the float chamber is coupled to the depression area

name: scan0060-text-0569
text: in the mixing chamber by means of a duct known as a

name: scan0060-text-0570
text: “suction hole”; this duct is controlled by a cock and

name: scan0060-text-0571
text: lever. At ground level the suction hole is shut: the

name: scan0060-text-0572
text: float chamber receives air at atmospheric pressure

name: scan0060-text-0573
text: through the leak hole: the maximum contrast exists

name: scan0060-text-0574
text: between the air pressures in the float and mixing cham-

name: scan0060-text-0575
text: bers, respectively: and the full petrol supply is obtained.

name: scan0060-text-0576
text: As the aeroplane climbs, and a reduction in the petrol

name: scan0060-text-0577
text: supply becomes essential, the suction hole is progressively

name: scan0060-text-0578
text: opened by means of the cock. The pressure in the

name: scan0060-text-0579
text: float chamber is proportionately reduced; and the petrol

name: scan0060-text-0580
text: supply is correspondingly cut down. Figs. 48-50 illus-

name: scan0060-text-0581
text: trate the manner in which this system is applied to the

name: scan0060-text-0583
text: The cock should always be kept closed at ground

name: scan0060-text-0584
text: level: otherwise the weak mixture will overheat the

name: scan0060-text-0585
text: engine, and, in addition, there is real danger of fire if

name: scan0060-text-0586
text: the cock is opened wide for more than a few seconds.

name: scan0060-text-0587
text: Fig. 48.

name: scan0060-text-0588
text: Diagram of the H.C. 7 Altitude Control.

name: scan0060-text-0589
text: F—Float chamber.

name: scan0060-text-0590
text: V—Control cock.

name: scan0060-text-0591
text: D—Air lead to float chamber.

name: scan0060-text-0592
text: P1—Leak hole.

name: scan0060-text-0593
text: P2—Suction hole.

name: scan0061-text-0002
text: Judicious use of the control will begin to make an

name: scan0061-text-0003
text: appreciable difference in power and revolutions when a

name: scan0061-text-0004
text: height of 10,000 feet is exceeded. At lower altitudes the

name: scan0061-text-0005
text: control will effect real fuel economies, even if its use is

name: scan0061-text-0006
text: not reflected on the tachometer dial.

name: scan0061-text-0007
text: The control, if already open, is automatically re-

name: scan0061-text-0008
text: turned to the shut position whenever the throttle is

name: scan0061-text-0009
text: closed. There is therefore no longer any risk of the

name: scan0061-text-0010
text: engine being starved through the control being open

name: scan0061-text-0011
text: when the pilot flattens out after a long dive. On the other

name: scan0061-text-0012
text: hand, pilots should remember to reopen the control after

name: scan0061-text-0013
text: a dive which terminates at a high altitude, e.g.. after

name: scan0061-text-0014
text: descending from 20,000 feet to 15,000 feet; otherwise,

name: scan0061-text-0015
text: the mixture will be excessively rich when the engine is

name: scan0061-text-0016
text: accelerated.

name: scan0061-text-0017
text: Fig. 49.

name: scan0061-text-0018
text: Diagram illustrating three positions of H.C. 7

name: scan0061-text-0019
text: Altitude Control Cock.

name: scan0061-text-0020
text: Top: Suction holes shut.

name: scan0061-text-0021
text: Centre: Suction holes just opening.

name: scan0061-text-0022
text: Bottom: Suction holes at maximum opening.

name: scan0062-text-0024
text: It is obviously impossible to recommend definite

name: scan0062-text-0025
text: positions of the lever for specific altitudes. As a general

name: scan0062-text-0026
text: rule, pilots will make a practice of opening the control

name: scan0062-text-0027
text: as far as is possible without sacrificing revolutions.

name: scan0062-text-0028
text: Fig. 50.

name: scan0062-text-0029
text: Photograph of H.C. 7 Altitude Control Cock.

name: scan0063-text-0031
text: CHAPTER IV.

name: scan0063-text-0032
text: IGNITION.

name: scan0063-text-0033
text: THE GENERATOR.

name: scan0063-text-0034
text: The ignition system is a highly developed form of

name: scan0063-text-0035
text: battery-coil ignition, designed as an integral part of the

name: scan0063-text-0036
text: engine. Owing to the angle between the two banks of

name: scan0063-text-0037
text: cylinders being 45°, it is not possible to use a conven-

name: scan0063-text-0038
text: tional type of 12-cylinder magneto, and although various

name: scan0063-text-0039
text: schemes for the use of magnetos were considered, the

name: scan0063-text-0040
text: present arrangement was finally adopted as providing the

name: scan0063-text-0041
text: best compromise and being capable of rapid production.

name: scan0063-text-0042
text: The general lay-out comprises a direct current

name: scan0063-text-0043
text: dynamo-generator, gear driven from the engine, and

name: scan0063-text-0044
text: charging an 8-volt accumulator battery: current is sup-

name: scan0063-text-0045
text: plied by the generator or battery to two complete ignition

name: scan0063-text-0046
text: units which are mounted on the rear ends of the two

name: scan0063-text-0047
text: camshafts. The necessary switches and instruments are

name: scan0063-text-0048
text: made up into a neat switch-board, and carried in the

name: scan0063-text-0049
text: pilot’s cockpit. Each ignition unit consists of a contact

name: scan0063-text-0050
text: breaker for the low tension primary current, an induc-

name: scan0063-text-0051
text: tion coil in which high tension current is induced at the

name: scan0063-text-0052
text: moment of “break,” and a distributor which passes the

name: scan0063-text-0053
text: H.T. current to the plugs in their proper sequence.

name: scan0063-text-0054
text: Each ignition unit is complete in itself as regards the

name: scan0063-text-0055
text: contact breaker mechanism, the coil, and the distributor,

name: scan0063-text-0056
text: and each unit fires a plug in each cylinder. So far as

name: scan0063-text-0057
text: this portion of the system goes, there is absolute dupli-

name: scan0063-text-0058
text: cation, with a further duplication of the main contact

name: scan0063-text-0059
text: breaker levers—as described in detail later.

name: scan0063-text-0060
text: Current for ignition is supplied at starting, or when

name: scan0063-text-0061
text: running with only one unit switched on, by the battery.

name: scan0063-text-0062
text: As soon as the engine has run up to about 650 r.p.m. the

name: scan0063-text-0063
text: generator takes up the ignition load, and on a further

name: scan0063-text-0064
text: increase of speed begins to charge the battery, which is

name: scan0063-text-0065
text: thus kept in good condition and well charged. In the

name: scan0063-text-0066
text: event of a breakdown of the battery, the generator will

name: scan0063-text-0067
text: run the ignition service, but the engine cannot then be

name: scan0063-text-0068
text: restarted after a stop.

name: scan0063-text-0069
text: The generator, Fig. 51, is of the 4-pole, totally en-

name: scan0063-text-0070
text: closed type, shunt wound for a maximum output of about

name: scan0063-text-0071
text: 15 amperes at 10 volts, the normal output being consider-

name: scan0063-text-0072
text: ably lower, or about 5 amperes. In constructional

name: scan0063-text-0073
text: details the generator is quite simple; the tubular steel

name: scan0063-text-0074
text: yoke A is held between cast aluminium end shields or

name: scan0063-text-0075
text: housings B-C, which are bolted up with four long screws,

name: scan0063-text-0076
text: of which the heads are locked by a simple ring of steel

name: scan0063-text-0077
text: wire, D. The armature runs in a ball bearing in the

name: scan0064-text-0079
text: Fig. 51.

name: scan0064-text-0080
text: The Generator.

name: scan0065-text-0082
text: upper or brush-gear end shield, but the driving end is

name: scan0065-text-0083
text: merely steadied by a plain bush containing a felt oil

name: scan0065-text-0084
text: retaining washer. The driving end shield B is provided

name: scan0065-text-0085
text: with three lugs by which the generator is studded down

name: scan0065-text-0086
text: to the crankcase between the cylinders, and is extended

name: scan0065-text-0087
text: to accommodate a pair of spiral gears which serve to

name: scan0065-text-0088
text: drive the revolution indicator. The armature is built up

name: scan0065-text-0089
text: of the usual laminations upon a steel spindle, the driving

name: scan0065-text-0090
text: end of the latter being splined to fit a corresponding

name: scan0065-text-0091
text: socket on the driving gear shaft, which runs in ball

name: scan0065-text-0092
text: bearings mounted in the crankcase. No unusual pre-

name: scan0065-text-0093
text: cautions are required when mounting or dismounting the

name: scan0065-text-0094
text: generator, but care should be taken to see that the splined

name: scan0065-text-0095
text: spindle end is not burred or damaged before assembly.

name: scan0065-text-0096
text: The revolution indicator drive gear E must be unscrewed

name: scan0065-text-0097
text: complete before the armature can be withdrawn.

name: scan0065-text-0098
text: The armature is wound with 21 coils in series, the

name: scan0065-text-0099
text: conductors being double-cotton-covered copper, with 20

name: scan0065-text-0100
text: wires per slot total. The commutator has 21 sections,

name: scan0065-text-0101
text: and is 1

name: scan0065-text-0105
text: in. in diameter. The four field coils each con-

name: scan0065-text-0106
text: sist of 145 turns of single-cotton-covered copper, the

name: scan0065-text-0107
text: resistance being approximately

name: scan0065-text-0111
text: ohm per coil at 60° F.

name: scan0065-text-0112
text: Two of the carbon brushes are insulated, but the

name: scan0065-text-0113
text: other two are earthed: the whole system is connected

name: scan0065-text-0114
text: up with one side insulated and the other earthed, a

name: scan0065-text-0115
text: method which results in a considerable simplification of

name: scan0065-text-0116
text: wiring and detail work. The details of the brush

name: scan0065-text-0117
text: gear are extremely simple, the brushes being held

name: scan0065-text-0118
text: up to their work by helical springs, which should

name: scan0065-text-0119
text: maintain a practically constant pressure throughout

name: scan0065-text-0120
text: the life of the brushes, the correct load being

name: scan0065-text-0121
text: from 1 to 1

name: scan0065-text-0125
text: lb. per brush. The brush gear is

name: scan0065-text-0126
text: enclosed by a light pressed aluminium cover F, through

name: scan0065-text-0127
text: which the two cable terminal studs project: one of these,

name: scan0065-text-0128
text: G, is connected to the insulated brushes, and is marked

name: scan0065-text-0129
text: “GEN. ARM”; the other, H, takes the field current,

name: scan0065-text-0130
text: and is marked “GEN. FIELD.” The end of the cover

name: scan0065-text-0131
text: is lined with insulating sheet, but some early models have

name: scan0065-text-0132
text: a couple of loose fibre caps to protect the brush gear

name: scan0065-text-0133
text: stud ends, instead of a complete lining.

name: scan0065-text-0134
text: Practically the only attention required by the genera-

name: scan0065-text-0135
text: tor should be cleaning of the commutator, and an occa-

name: scan0065-text-0136
text: sional drop or two of thick oil to the ball bearing at the

name: scan0065-text-0137
text: upper end of the spindle. At intervals corresponding to

name: scan0065-text-0138
text: the stripping of the engine, the brush gear should be

name: scan0065-text-0139
text: carefully looked over, and any necessary adjustments

name: scan0065-text-0140
text: made; the windings should be well dusted by the use of

name: scan0065-text-0141
text: bellows or an air jet; and the revolution indicator drive

name: scan0065-text-0142
text: repacked with grease. The commutator must be watched

name: scan0065-text-0143
text: for signs of scoring or unevenness of the bars: it should

name: scan0066-text-0145
text: THE VOLTAGE REGULATOR.

name: scan0066-text-0146
text: be trued up in the lathe before being allowed to become

name: scan0066-text-0147
text: really bad. Should the insulating material between the

name: scan0066-text-0148
text: copper bars tend to stand proud of the surface, it should

name: scan0066-text-0149
text: be carefully scraped down by the use of a keen hooked

name: scan0066-text-0150
text: scraper tool, which may conveniently be made from a

name: scan0066-text-0151
text: hacksaw blade. The commutator and brushes should

name: scan0066-text-0152
text: become nicely glazed, and this condition is not to be

name: scan0066-text-0153
text: interefered with. New brushes must be fitted by rubbing

name: scan0066-text-0154
text: them down on a strip of fine glass paper wrapped round

name: scan0066-text-0155
text: the commutator, so as to bring them to the proper

name: scan0066-text-0156
text: section. To do this, one of the four long assembly

name: scan0066-text-0157
text: screws should be removed, when a brush arm may be

name: scan0066-text-0158
text: lifted well clear of the commutator.

name: scan0066-text-0159
text: In the field no attempt should be made to effect any

name: scan0066-text-0160
text: actual repairs to the generator in the shape of re-winding

name: scan0066-text-0161
text: and so on; such work is for experts at base depôts only.

name: scan0066-text-0162
text: No provision is made in the generator itself to effect

name: scan0066-text-0163
text: any regulation of the voltage or current output under

name: scan0066-text-0164
text: varying conditions of load or speed, but an automatic

name: scan0066-text-0165
text: device is employed to regulate the voltage, and conse-

name: scan0066-text-0166
text: quently the current, by intermittently breaking the direct

name: scan0066-text-0167
text: earth connection of the field winding, thereby weakening

name: scan0066-text-0168
text: the field and keeping the voltage down to the desired

name: scan0066-text-0169
text: value.

name: scan0066-text-0170
text: Fig. 52.

name: scan0066-text-0171
text: Voltage Regulator.

name: scan0067-text-0173
text: The regulator, Fig. 52, is mounted within a cast

name: scan0067-text-0174
text: aluminium cup A, which normally is fixed behind the

name: scan0067-text-0175
text: switchboard. It consists of a soft iron core wound with

name: scan0067-text-0176
text: three windings of differing natures, magnetisation of the

name: scan0067-text-0177
text: core due to the flow of current in these windings serving

name: scan0067-text-0178
text: to pull down an “armature” blade B, and so break the

name: scan0067-text-0179
text: direct path to earth for the field current. When the

name: scan0067-text-0180
text: generator is not running, or when its voltage is below

name: scan0067-text-0181
text: that to which the regulator is set—say 10 volts, the pair

name: scan0067-text-0182
text: of contacts C are closed, and the field current can pass to

name: scan0067-text-0183
text: earth across them. As the voltage rises, however, the

name: scan0067-text-0184
text: pull of the core opposes, and eventually overcomes that

name: scan0067-text-0185
text: of the spring D, resulting in the opening of the contacts at

name: scan0067-text-0186
text: C. The alternative path for the field current is through

name: scan0067-text-0187
text: two of the coils wound upon the core, one of these being

name: scan0067-text-0188
text: of 115 ohms resistance, and the other—wound non-induc-

name: scan0067-text-0189
text: tively—of 44 ohms. There is, therefore, a resistance of

name: scan0067-text-0190
text: 159 ohms inserted into the field circuit by the opening

name: scan0067-text-0191
text: of the contacts, the result naturally being an immediate

name: scan0067-text-0192
text: fall in the current flowing in the circuit, and a corre-

name: scan0067-text-0193
text: sponding weakening of the field.

name: scan0067-text-0194
text: Adjustment of the regulator to maintain any line

name: scan0067-text-0195
text: voltage within limits is made by changing the tension

name: scan0067-text-0196
text: on the spring D; tightening up the nut E raises, and

name: scan0067-text-0197
text: slackening it off reduces, the voltage. In making the

name: scan0067-text-0198
text: adjustment, only the nut is to be turned upon the screw,

name: scan0067-text-0199
text: the latter being held by the knurled head F while the nut

name: scan0067-text-0200
text: is turned. The correct gap of the contact points C is

name: scan0067-text-0201
text: from .005 to .007 in. when the armature blade B is pulled

name: scan0067-text-0202
text: down upon the stop pin; the pin projects from .043 to

name: scan0067-text-0203
text: .045 in. beyond the end of the core. It is important to

name: scan0067-text-0204
text: maintain the correct setting of the gaps, as successful

name: scan0067-text-0205
text: operation will depend largely upon the air gap in the

name: scan0067-text-0206
text: magnetic circuit when the contacts are closed. In action,

name: scan0067-text-0207
text: the armature blade is in a state of continual movement,

name: scan0067-text-0208
text: the contacts opening and closing rapidly—just like those

name: scan0067-text-0209
text: of a trembler coil or a bell. The adjustable contact screw

name: scan0067-text-0210
text: is locked by a spot of solder, and requires touching only

name: scan0067-text-0211
text: at quite long intervals.

name: scan0067-text-0212
text: The sole attention the regulator should need is

name: scan0067-text-0213
text: periodic cleaning and adjustment of the contacts, and

name: scan0067-text-0214
text: light lubrication of the bearing on which the armature

name: scan0067-text-0215
text: oscillates.

name: scan0067-text-0216
text: As the regulator is very inaccessible when fitted

name: scan0067-text-0217
text: behind the switchboard, a large opening must be cut in

name: scan0067-text-0218
text: the wood board on which the two are mounted, as indi-

name: scan0067-text-0219
text: cated by the dotted line A of Fig. 55, so at to permit of

name: scan0067-text-0220
text: access to the contacts after the switchboard has been

name: scan0068-text-0222
text: Fig. 53

name: scan0068-text-0223
text: Front of Switchboard.

name: scan0068-text-0224
text: Fig. 54.

name: scan0068-text-0225
text: Back of Switchboard.

name: scan0068-text-0226
text: A—To positive terminal battery (use heavy cable).

name: scan0068-text-0227
text: C—To right-hand ignition unit.

name: scan0068-text-0228
text: D—To left-hand ignition unit.

name: scan0068-text-0229
text: B—To terminal marked “GEN. ARM.” on voltage

name: scan0068-text-0230
text: regulator, and thence to generator (use heavy

name: scan0068-text-0231
text: cable).

name: scan0069-text-0233
text: THE SWITCHBOARD.

name: scan0069-text-0234
text: removed. To remove the switchboard it is necessary to

name: scan0069-text-0235
text: take off the nuts on the two studs at B. The regulator and

name: scan0069-text-0236
text: switchboard are delivered assembled on a piece of

name: scan0069-text-0240
text: in.

name: scan0069-text-0241
text: wood, which represents the instrument board or special

name: scan0069-text-0242
text: base upon which they are to be permanently mounted in

name: scan0069-text-0243
text: the aircraft. When fixing the regulator, the fanged

name: scan0069-text-0244
text: washers C provided are to be fitted as indicated, the lugs

name: scan0069-text-0245
text: being turned up against flats on the nuts after the latter

name: scan0069-text-0246
text: have pulled the fangs into the wood.

name: scan0069-text-0247
text: The switchboard, of which front and back views

name: scan0069-text-0248
text: are shown in Figs. 53 and 54, consists of a metal pressing

name: scan0069-text-0249
text: and a moulding of insulating material held together by

name: scan0069-text-0250
text: the two long studs which fix the regulator, and by a

name: scan0069-text-0251
text: screw set between the switch handles. The two switches

name: scan0069-text-0252
text: control the two ignition units, and serve at the same time

name: scan0069-text-0253
text: to connect the generator to the battery for charging;

name: scan0069-text-0254
text: the generator-to-battery circuit being completed only

name: scan0069-text-0255
text: when both switches are in the “on” position together.

name: scan0069-text-0256
text: Above the switches, and permanently connected up by

name: scan0069-text-0257
text: metal strips, is a central-zero Weston ammeter reading

name: scan0069-text-0258
text: to 20 amperes, charge and discharge.

name: scan0069-text-0259
text: Fig. 55

name: scan0069-text-0260
text: Mounting of Switchboard and Voltage Regulator.

name: scan0069-text-0261
text: A—Cut hole in wood as shown by dotted line.

name: scan0069-text-0262
text: B—Two bolt holes,

name: scan0069-text-0266
text: in. diameter.

name: scan0069-text-0267
text: C—When permanently fixed, bend up one ear of

name: scan0069-text-0268
text: tab-washer against nut.

name: scan0070-text-0270
text: The ammeter shows the net current passing to or

name: scan0070-text-0271
text: from the battery: when it indicates zero with the engine

name: scan0070-text-0272
text: running and both switches on, the generator will actually

name: scan0070-text-0273
text: be supplying about 3 amperes to the two ignition systems,

name: scan0070-text-0274
text: and 3 amperes must be added to all “charge” readings to

name: scan0070-text-0275
text: get the true value of the generator output. If both

name: scan0070-text-0276
text: switches be put to “on” before the engine has run up to

name: scan0070-text-0277
text: about 650 r.p.m., the battery will discharge through the

name: scan0070-text-0278
text: generator, as the voltage of the latter will be lower than

name: scan0070-text-0279
text: that of the battery. The difficulty arises, however, that

name: scan0070-text-0280
text: if the engine be started up on one ignition only, the other

name: scan0070-text-0281
text: set of plugs are likely to become oiled up badly by the

name: scan0070-text-0282
text: time the engine can be run up to the speed at which the

name: scan0070-text-0283
text: generator voltage will balance the battery voltage and

name: scan0070-text-0284
text: charging can commence. Therefore, after starting the

name: scan0070-text-0285
text: engine on one ignition unit only, the other unit must be

name: scan0070-text-0286
text: switched on at once to prevent the plugs fouling up.

name: scan0070-text-0287
text: This will result in the battery discharging for a time, the

name: scan0070-text-0288
text: rate depending upon the speed at which the engine is run.

name: scan0070-text-0289
text: Throttled right down to about 450 to 500 r.p.m., the dis-

name: scan0070-text-0290
text: charge rate will be 6 to 7 amperes, which will not harm the

name: scan0070-text-0291
text: battery, and may be maintained for as long as is neces-

name: scan0070-text-0292
text: sary to warm the engine up sufficiently to work it up to

name: scan0070-text-0293
text: a higher speed. It is of the utmost importance, however,

name: scan0070-text-0294
text: that only one ignition be switched on at starting, other-

name: scan0070-text-0295
text: wise the discharge rate may be as high as 30 amperes or

name: scan0070-text-0296
text: more, which will not only run the battery down very

name: scan0070-text-0297
text: quickly, but may actually do harm to the generator and

name: scan0070-text-0298
text: coils.

name: scan0070-text-0299
text: The switches are of a very simple pattern, and con-

name: scan0070-text-0300
text: sist of four-armed spiders riding over metal contact

name: scan0070-text-0301
text: studs set in the base moulding. There are two small

name: scan0070-text-0302
text: resistance units, consisting of nickel-chrome wire wound

name: scan0070-text-0303
text: upon grooved porcelain discs, mounted behind the

name: scan0070-text-0304
text: switches; the function of these is to keep down the

name: scan0070-text-0305
text: current passing through the ignition coils when the latter

name: scan0070-text-0306
text: are switched on with the engine standing. As the resis-

name: scan0070-text-0307
text: tance of the ignition coils is very low—about

name: scan0070-text-0311
text: ohm—the

name: scan0070-text-0312
text: current would be very high without these 1 ohm steadying

name: scan0070-text-0313
text: resistances, which keep the initial current down to about

name: scan0070-text-0314
text: 5 amperes per set. Should a switch be left on with the

name: scan0070-text-0315
text: engine standing, there will be no discharge unless the

name: scan0070-text-0316
text: contact breaker points are closed, but if the circuit be

name: scan0070-text-0317
text: completed the ammeter will read about 5 amperes,

name: scan0070-text-0318
text: gradually falling to about 3 amperes as the resistance

name: scan0070-text-0319
text: warms up. Should both switches be left on, the dis-

name: scan0070-text-0320
text: charge will be 30 amperes or so, and the battery will be

name: scan0070-text-0321
text: totally discharged in a few minutes.

name: scan0070-text-0322
text: The terminals for wiring up the switch are plainly

name: scan0071-text-0324
text: THE BATTERY.

name: scan0071-text-0325
text: marked, and the connections are indicated in the figure,

name: scan0071-text-0326
text: as well as in the general wiring diagram. Once in every

name: scan0071-text-0327
text: month the switches should be exposed and cleaned, and

name: scan0071-text-0328
text: a little grease smeared on the track over which the con-

name: scan0071-text-0329
text: tacts move. At the same time, the two resistances should

name: scan0071-text-0330
text: be examined: if they have been overheated the coils

name: scan0071-text-0331
text: may have become unevenly spaced, or even come into

name: scan0071-text-0332
text: contact in places. If they cannot be neatly opened out

name: scan0071-text-0333
text: to even spacing, new coils must be fitted at once, as any

name: scan0071-text-0334
text: fault here may have serious consequences. Should a

name: scan0071-text-0335
text: resistance burn out or break, it will cut off that ignition;

name: scan0071-text-0336
text: should several of the coils touch, the resistance may be

name: scan0071-text-0337
text: so reduced that burning of the contact breaker points

name: scan0071-text-0338
text: may take place, or even a burn-out in the coil.

name: scan0071-text-0339
text: The standard 8-volt Liberty battery. of Willard or

name: scan0071-text-0340
text: Exide make consists of four cells in a one-piece ebonite

name: scan0071-text-0341
text: box, measuring approximately 5

name: scan0071-text-0345
text: in. long by 3

name: scan0071-text-0349
text: in. wide

name: scan0071-text-0350
text: by 6

name: scan0071-text-0354
text: in. high to top of terminals. The battery is of the

name: scan0071-text-0355
text: so-called “unspillable” type, but is not absolutely so: it

name: scan0071-text-0356
text: is quite sufficiently so for all practical purposes, however.

name: scan0071-text-0357
text: Fig. 56 shows a section through an end cell of a Willard

name: scan0071-text-0358

name: scan0071-text-0360

name: scan0072-text-0363
text: plates B-C rest, with a fair amount of sludge space below

name: scan0072-text-0364
text: them; it is provided with a main lid D, and a baffle plate

name: scan0072-text-0365
text: E, sealed in with the usual compound at F. The baffle

name: scan0072-text-0366
text: plate has a standpipe vent at G, and a small acid drain

name: scan0072-text-0367
text: hole at H; the filler vent plug I screws down on a rubber

name: scan0072-text-0368
text: joint ring, and is sufficiently long to stand above the

text: electrolyte if the battery is turned upside down until all

name: scan0072-text-0370
text: the acid has drained from the main compartment in which

name: scan0072-text-0371
text: the plates are. The normal acid level is just below the

name: scan0072-text-0372
text: baffle plate, and one cannot judge by mere inspection

name: scan0072-text-0373
text: whether there is plenty of acid or a considerable shortage.

name: scan0072-text-0374

text: INSTRUCTIONS FOR PREPARING BATTERY

name: scan0073-text-0379

text: INSTRUCTIONS FOR MAINTENANCE IN

name: scan0073-text-0381
text: SERVICE.

name: scan0073-text-0382
text: The makers’ detailed instructions for care of these

name: scan0073-text-0383
text: batteries are as follows:—

name: scan0073-text-0384
text: (1) Remove the vent plug.

name: scan0073-text-0385
text: (2) With the syringe provided in crate, fill each

name: scan0073-text-0386
text: cell to a depth of 1 in. over the baffle plate (see Fig.

name: scan0073-text-0387
text: 57) with electrolyte taken from the glass bottle

name: scan0073-text-0388
text: provided in crate.

name: scan0073-text-0389
text: (3) After fifteen minutes, check to see that elec-

name: scan0073-text-0390
text: trolyte is 1 in. above the baffle plate (using a glass

name: scan0073-text-0391
text: tube as shown in Fig. 57). If the electrolyte is not

name: scan0073-text-0392
text: 1 in. above the baffle plate, additional electrolyte

name: scan0073-text-0393
text: should be added. A glass tube is provided in the

name: scan0073-text-0394
text: crate.

name: scan0073-text-0395
text: (4) Allow the battery to cool for eight hours.

name: scan0073-text-0396
text: (5) Charge the battery at 0.7 ampere for 70 hours.

name: scan0073-text-0397
text: (6) Take a test discharge of 20 amperes from the

name: scan0073-text-0398
text: battery for fifteen seconds, each cell voltage to be

name: scan0073-text-0399
text: taken immediately. If each cell is 1.55 volts, or

name: scan0073-text-0400
text: above (at 80° F.), with the above current flowing,

name: scan0073-text-0401
text: battery is O.K.

name: scan0073-text-0402
text: (7) Allow the battery to stand for fifteen minutes;

name: scan0073-text-0403
text: then, with the syringe mentioned above, remove sur-

name: scan0073-text-0404
text: plus electrolyte from each cell down to the baffle

name: scan0073-text-0405
text: plate, the battery being in upright position. (See

name: scan0073-text-0407
text: Battery should be flushed once a week, as fol-

name: scan0073-text-0408
text: lows:—Vent plug should be removed and each cell

name: scan0073-text-0409
text: filled with distilled water to a height of 1 in. above

name: scan0073-text-0410
text: the baffle plate “E,” as shown in cross section of

name: scan0073-text-0411
text: Fig. 57, allowed to stand for a minimum of two

name: scan0073-text-0412
text: minutes (not over five minutes), and take off surplus

name: scan0073-text-0413
text: water down to plate “E” with hydrometer syringe,

name: scan0073-text-0414
text: as shown in Fig. 58.

name: scan0073-text-0415
text: Specific gravity can be read and adjusted in the

name: scan0073-text-0416
text: following manner:—

name: scan0073-text-0417
text: (1) Battery should be flushed, as described above.

name: scan0073-text-0418
text: (2) If battery is in a discharged condition, it

name: scan0073-text-0419
text: should be put on charge at 1 ampere, and charged

name: scan0075-text-0428
text: FITTING THE BATTERY.

name: scan0075-text-0429
text: until the terminal voltage with this current flowing

name: scan0075-text-0430
text: has risen to a maximum, i.e., shown no rise for a

name: scan0075-text-0431
text: period of one hour. (Vent plug should be left out

name: scan0075-text-0432
text: during this charge.) The battery should then be

name: scan0075-text-0433
text: tipped on its side and gravity taken with the hydro-

name: scan0075-text-0434
text: meter provided with a bent, hard rubber tube, as

name: scan0075-text-0435
text: shown in Fig. 59. Be sure to return electrolyte to

text: the cell from which it was taken.

name: scan0075-text-0437
text: In batteries fully charged, gravity should be

name: scan0075-text-0438
text: between 1.290 and 1.310. If gravity is not correct

text: on taking gravity readings, battery should be held

name: scan0075-text-0440
text: upside down for five or six minutes and electrolyte

name: scan0075-text-0441
text: allowed to run into a rubber or glass jar. The elec-

name: scan0075-text-0442
text: trolyte removed should be adjusted to 1.300 specific

text: gravity by the addition of distilled water, or 1.400

text: acid, as the case may be; then each cell should be

name: scan0075-text-0445
text: filled with this electrolyte until the level is 1 in. above

name: scan0078-text-0483
text: THE IGNITION UNITS.

name: scan0078-text-0484
text: In Fig. 60 is shown an ignition unit in its place upon

name: scan0078-text-0485
text: the engine, the distributor head having been removed to

name: scan0078-text-0486
text: expose the contact breakers. A detailed description

name: scan0078-text-0487
text: follows, the like parts having like reference letters in the

name: scan0078-text-0488
text: several figures.

name: scan0078-text-0489
text: At the rear end of each camshaft housing there is

name: scan0078-text-0490
text: a flange with six bolts to take the corresponding flanged

name: scan0078-text-0491
text: base A of the contact breaker shown in detail in Fig. 61.

name: scan0078-text-0492
text: The six bolt holes are slotted to permit of the base plate

name: scan0078-text-0493
text: A being adjusted 10° relatively to the camshaft casing,

name: scan0078-text-0494
text: so providing for fine setting of the ignition timing.

name: scan0078-text-0495
text: Mounted upon the base plate A is the base B of the con-

name: scan0078-text-0496
text: tact breaker proper: the back of B is shown in Fig. 62,

name: scan0078-text-0497
text: with four studs C which pass through slotted holes in

name: scan0078-text-0498
text: lugs cast on A. The slots are long enough to permit a

name: scan0078-text-0499
text: timing control movement of 20°, equal to 40° on the

name: scan0078-text-0500
text: crankshaft, and the movement is effected by the usual

name: scan0078-text-0501
text: Fig. 62.

name: scan0078-text-0502

text: (back view).

name: scan0079-text-0505
text: control lever coupled up to the arm D, which may be

name: scan0079-text-0506
text: reversed for use on either right- or left-hand units. The

name: scan0079-text-0507
text: base B has a brass-sleeved boss E, which registers A

name: scan0079-text-0508
text: and B concentrically; there is a thin brass friction washer

name: scan0079-text-0509
text: F to prevent the rub being between two aluminium sur-

name: scan0079-text-0510
text: faces. The studs C (Fig. 63) are provided with special

name: scan0079-text-0511
text: nuts with collars which pull up against springs, and with

name: scan0079-text-0512
text: fibre washers bearing on the back of the lugs cast on A;

name: scan0079-text-0513
text: the studs limit the travel, and the springs absorb chatter.

name: scan0079-text-0514
text: The nuts should be tightened up as far as they will go

name: scan0079-text-0515
text: without causing binding of the control gear.

name: scan0079-text-0516
text: Mounted in the base B are two annular ball bearings

name: scan0079-text-0517
text: provided with grease-retaining felt washers, and in these

name: scan0079-text-0518
text: bearings the cam spindle runs. In Fig. 64 the 12-lobed

name: scan0079-text-0519
text: Fig. 63.

text: Attachment of Contact Breaker Base (B)

name: scan0079-text-0521
text: to Main Flange (A).

name: scan0079-text-0523
text: The Cam and Cam Spindle.

name: scan0080-text-0525
text: cam G is seen apart from the spindle H, to which it is

name: scan0080-text-0526
text: keyed and secured by the screw I (Fig. 61); the screw

name: scan0080-text-0527
text: also retains the high tension distributor rotor J (Fig. 61)

name: scan0080-text-0528
text: in place, the rotor being driven by a shallow stud pro-

name: scan0080-text-0529
text: jecting from the cam disc. The thin dished flange K is

name: scan0080-text-0530
text: merely an oil thrower, to prevent an excessive amount

name: scan0080-text-0531
text: of oil working along from the camshaft housing into the

name: scan0080-text-0532
text: contact breaker. In early models, the cam spindle was

name: scan0080-text-0533
text: driven by a laminated spring coupling engaging with

name: scan0080-text-0534
text: slots in the camshaft end (Fig. 65), with a dowel peg to

name: scan0080-text-0535
text: take the drive in the event of the springs breaking. In

name: scan0080-text-0536
text: later models, the spring drive is dispensed with, and a

name: scan0080-text-0537
text: plain solid dowel peg engages a notch in a steel flange

name: scan0080-text-0538
text: nipped under the seven nuts which bolt up the driven

name: scan0080-text-0539
text: bevel wheel to the camshaft (Fig. 66).

name: scan0080-text-0540
text: The body of the cam is hollowed out from the back

name: scan0080-text-0541
text: and filled in with a felt oil pad, held in place by a light

name: scan0080-text-0542
text: pressed steel plate. In the face of the cam there is a hole

name: scan0080-text-0543
text: through which the felt may be oiled, and six tiny holes,

name: scan0080-text-0544
text: drilled radially through the broad noses of the cam, feed

name: scan0080-text-0545
text: oil to the fibre striker pads of the contact breaker levers.

name: scan0080-text-0546
text: As the merest trace of oiliness is sufficient for these, care

name: scan0080-text-0547
text: Fig. 65.

name: scan0080-text-0548
text: Cam Spindle Drive

name: scan0080-text-0549
text: (early pattern).

name: scan0081-text-0002
text: THE CONTACT BREAKERS.

name: scan0081-text-0003
text: should be taken not to overdo the oiling here: it may

name: scan0081-text-0004
text: be found that no special provision was necessary after

name: scan0081-text-0005
text: all. The cam has six broad and six narrow noses or

name: scan0081-text-0006
text: lobes, corresponding to the angular intervals between

name: scan0081-text-0007
text: firing points—namely, 75° and 45° successively.

name: scan0081-text-0008
text: On the external face of the base plate B (Fig. 61)

name: scan0081-text-0009
text: there is mounted a pressed steel ring L carrying the

name: scan0081-text-0010
text: earthed contacts, the three insulated contact breaker

name: scan0081-text-0011
text: levers, and the condenser M. The ring L is pivotted on

name: scan0081-text-0012
text: a stud to the right of the condenser, and has three other

name: scan0081-text-0013
text: holes which are slotted for two plain studs and a screwed

name: scan0081-text-0014
text: stud; the screwed stud is to the left of the condenser, and

name: scan0081-text-0015
text: has a nut and split pin. The ring can, therefore, be

name: scan0081-text-0016
text: moved slightly in relation to the cam in order to correct

name: scan0081-text-0017
text: the setting of the contact breakers. There is also an

name: scan0081-text-0018
text: insulated half-ring N, carrying the ends of the three

name: scan0081-text-0019
text: spring blades controlling the levers, and the small resis-

name: scan0081-text-0020
text: tance coil O. One end of the half-ring N is connected

name: scan0081-text-0021
text: Fig. 66.

name: scan0081-text-0022
text: Cam Spindle Drive

name: scan0081-text-0023
text: (later pattern).

name: scan0082-text-0025
text: to the insulated stud P, and primary current from the

name: scan0082-text-0026
text: generator or battery (after passing the coil) goes to earth

name: scan0082-text-0027
text: via this connection, the springs, and the levers and con-

name: scan0082-text-0028
text: tacts. At Q there is another insulated stud to which the

name: scan0082-text-0029
text: primary lead from the switch is connected, and which,

name: scan0082-text-0030
text: with its fellow P, serves to secure the distributor, and

name: scan0082-text-0031
text: at the same time makes the primary circuit complete

name: scan0082-text-0032
text: through the coil. The distributor cap is held in place

name: scan0082-text-0033
text: by four spring-clips R in addition to these two studs, but

name: scan0082-text-0034
text: the knurled-headed socket nuts of the studs P-Q must be

name: scan0082-text-0035
text: pulled down very tight to make a good electrical circuit,

name: scan0082-text-0036
text: apart from the mere holding of the distributor.

name: scan0082-text-0037
text: The arrangement of the three contact breaker

name: scan0082-text-0038
text: levers presents several novel features, and must

name: scan0082-text-0039
text: be described at some length. To secure an

name: scan0082-text-0040
text: increased measure of reliability, two main contact

name: scan0082-text-0041
text: breaker levers S-S (Fig. 61), are provided, either

name: scan0082-text-0042
text: one of which will operate the ignition in the

name: scan0082-text-0043
text: event of a failure of the other. Probably the

name: scan0082-text-0044
text: most likely lever of the three to break down is the small

name: scan0082-text-0045
text: auxiliary one T, and if this fail the other two may

name: scan0082-text-0046
text: become useless, depending upon the nature of the fault.

name: scan0082-text-0047
text: Should it remain permanently closed, the main levers

name: scan0082-text-0048
text: cannot break the circuit, but if the auxiliary lever should

name: scan0082-text-0049
text: open and remain open, the operation of the main levers

name: scan0082-text-0050
text: will not be interfered with. In any case should one of

name: scan0082-text-0051
text: the main levers, or the auxiliary lever, break down, it

name: scan0082-text-0052
text: may be removed, and the engine run on one main lever

name: scan0082-text-0053
text: only.

name: scan0082-text-0054
text: Fig. 67.

name: scan0082-text-0055
text: A Main Contact Breaker Lever.

name: scan0083-text-0057
text: THE HIGH TENSION DISTRIBUTOR.

name: scan0083-text-0058
text: A main contact breaker lever S is shown apart in

name: scan0083-text-0059
text: Fig. 67; the fibre striker pad U, the rivetted-in tungsten

name: scan0083-text-0060
text: contact V, and the vulcanised-in rubber buffer pad W

name: scan0083-text-0061
text: upon which the end of the spring X rests, are all clearly

name: scan0083-text-0062
text: seen. The auxiliary lever T (Fig. 61) is generally

name: scan0083-text-0063
text: similar, but cranked instead of straight, and the spring

name: scan0083-text-0064
text: is connected to a small resistance coil O of about

name: scan0083-text-0065
text: 8 ohms, instead of direct to the half-ring N already

name: scan0083-text-0066
text: described. This auxiliary lever is timed about 5° in

name: scan0083-text-0067
text: advance of the main levers, both for opening and

name: scan0083-text-0068
text: closing.

name: scan0083-text-0069
text: When running normally in the forward direction

name: scan0083-text-0070
text: (which is clockwise as viewed from the face of the unit),

name: scan0083-text-0071
text: the sequence of operation is thus: (a), all contacts closed

name: scan0083-text-0072
text: and current flowing; (b), auxiliary contacts open, and

name: scan0083-text-0073
text: current flows across main contacts only; (c), main con-

name: scan0083-text-0074
text: tacts open, circuit is broken, and spark occurs; (d),

name: scan0083-text-0075
text: auxiliary contacts close, and current flows through the

name: scan0083-text-0076
text: resistance coil; (e), main contacts close, and current flows

name: scan0083-text-0077
text: across these almost exclusively, as they offer a path of

name: scan0083-text-0078
text: negligible resistance; (f), the cycle now recommences.

name: scan0083-text-0079
text: Should the engine try to run backwards, the ignition

name: scan0083-text-0080
text: is not actually cut out, but the flow of current (or, rather,

name: scan0083-text-0081
text: the change of rate of flow) at each break of the contacts

name: scan0083-text-0082
text: is so reduced that no spark can occur. The sequence on

name: scan0083-text-0083
text: reversal is:—(a), all contacts closed, and current flowing;

name: scan0083-text-0084
text: (b), main contacts open, but no spark occurs because the

name: scan0083-text-0085
text: circuit is closed through the alternative path offered by

name: scan0083-text-0086
text: the auxiliary contacts and the resistance, and consequently

name: scan0083-text-0087
text: the current in the coil winding, does not fall sufficiently

name: scan0083-text-0088
text: rapidly to induce a high voltage in the secondary winding;

name: scan0083-text-0089
text: (c), auxiliary contacts open, and again there is no spark,

name: scan0083-text-0090
text: because the current flow is at a very low value; (d), main

name: scan0083-text-0091
text: contacts close, and current flows; (e), auxiliary contacts

name: scan0083-text-0092
text: close; (f), the cycle now recommences. The auxiliary

name: scan0083-text-0093
text: contact breaker fills its function as a safety back-firing

name: scan0083-text-0094
text: device perfectly, with the qualification that it cannot pre-

name: scan0083-text-0095
text: vent a single back-fire if the circuit is broken when the

name: scan0083-text-0096
text: crank is in advance of top dead centre.

name: scan0083-text-0097
text: The distributor head (Figs. 68 and 69) is an ex-

name: scan0083-text-0098
text: tremely fine piece of moulding in the insulating material

name: scan0083-text-0099
text: known as Bakelite, a ring of different composition being

name: scan0083-text-0100
text: moulded in to form the rubbing track for the carbon

name: scan0083-text-0101
text: brush Z of the rotor J (seen in Fig. 61). The distributor

name: scan0083-text-0102
text: head has a spigot edge fitting into a bored register on

name: scan0083-text-0103
text: the contact breaker base (B, Fig. 61); it is firmly held in

name: scan0083-text-0104
text: place by four spring clips (R, Fig. 61), and two insulated

name: scan0084-text-0106
text: knurled headed socket nuts which screw down on to

name: scan0084-text-0107
text: the insulated studs P and Q (Fig. 61).

name: scan0084-text-0108
text: Fitting snugly into the domed head is the induction

name: scan0084-text-0109
text: coil, one end of which can be seen in Fig. 68. The coil

name: scan0084-text-0110
text: is built up, as usual, with two windings of insulated

name: scan0084-text-0111
text: copper wire upon a core of soft iron; the two ends of

name: scan0084-text-0112
text: the primary winding are electrically connected to the

name: scan0084-text-0113
text: metal portions of the knurled nuts fixing the head. As

name: scan0084-text-0114
text: the battery lead is connected to the terminal stud Q,

name: scan0084-text-0115
text: and the terminal stud P is in connection with the con-

name: scan0084-text-0116
text: tact breakers, it follows that the primary winding of

name: scan0084-text-0117
text: the coil forms part of the complete circuit, and that

name: scan0084-text-0118
text: current will flow in the coil when either or all of the

name: scan0084-text-0119
text: contact breakers are closed and the switch is on. One

name: scan0084-text-0120
text: Fig. 68.

name: scan0084-text-0121
text: The Distributor Head

name: scan0084-text-0122
text: (exterior).

name: scan0085-text-0124
text: end of the secondary winding of many turns of fine

name: scan0085-text-0125
text: wire is connected to the primary winding, but the high

name: scan0085-text-0126
text: potential end is connected to a fixed carbon brush

name: scan0085-text-0127
text: projecting slightly from the centre of a disc of insulating

name: scan0085-text-0128
text: sheet, which closes the inside of the distributor head

name: scan0085-text-0129
text: and hides the coil. This brush, when the unit is

name: scan0085-text-0130
text: assembled, presses upon a light bowed steel spring

name: scan0085-text-0131
text: blade Y (Fig. 61), carried on the rotor J; as the free

name: scan0085-text-0132
text: end of the spring blade touches upon a brass liner into

name: scan0085-text-0133
text: which the carbon brush Z fits, the brush is brought into

name: scan0085-text-0134
text: connection with the secondary winding of the coil.

name: scan0085-text-0135
text: Moulded into the brush track in the distributor head

name: scan0085-text-0136
text: Fig. 69.

name: scan0085-text-0137
text: The Distributor Head

name: scan0085-text-0138
text: (interior).

name: scan0086-text-0140
text: HIGH TENSION CABLES.

name: scan0086-text-0141
text: there are twelve circular studs or “segments,” each in

name: scan0086-text-0142
text: connection with a screwed terminal knob, by which the

name: scan0086-text-0143
text: corresponding high tension sparking plug cable is

name: scan0086-text-0144
text: fixed. The bosses into which the insulated terminal

name: scan0086-text-0145
text: knobs are sunk are notched on one side to clear the

name: scan0086-text-0146
text: cables, and on the other side are very clearly marked

name: scan0086-text-0147
text: with the numbers of the plugs; each terminal is pro-

name: scan0086-text-0148
text: vided with a spring washer. It will be noticed that the

name: scan0086-text-0149
text: distributor segments are not placed equally round the

name: scan0086-text-0150
text: brush track; they are at angles corresponding to those

name: scan0086-text-0151
text: of the cams, so that the rotor brush must always be

name: scan0086-text-0152
text: upon a segment when the cams open the circuit by

name: scan0086-text-0153
text: breaking the contacts apart. The edge of the brush

name: scan0086-text-0154
text: track is bevelled, so that the head may be the more

name: scan0086-text-0155
text: readily slipped on over the carbon rotor brush; great

name: scan0086-text-0156
text: care is necessary when putting the head into place, or

name: scan0086-text-0157
text: the brush may be broken.

name: scan0086-text-0158
text: There is no special safety gap in the high tension

name: scan0086-text-0159
text: circuit, but there is an air gap of about 14 mm. between

name: scan0086-text-0160
text: the spring blade Y and the head of the screw I, which

name: scan0086-text-0161
text: fixes the rotor and cam to the cam spindle, and in the

name: scan0086-text-0162
text: event of excess potential in the coil winding (due, for

name: scan0086-text-0163
text: example, to a lead having come off a plug), a spark

name: scan0086-text-0164
text: may pass here and save the coil from a breakdown.

name: scan0086-text-0165
text: The twelve high tension cables for each distributor

name: scan0086-text-0166
text: go respectively to one plug in each cylinder, the left-

name: scan0086-text-0167
text: hand unit firing the forward set of plugs and the right-

name: scan0086-text-0168
text: hand unit firing the after set. The leads are of the usual

name: scan0086-text-0169
text: pattern of 7 to 7

name: scan0086-text-0173
text: mm. rubber insulated flexible cable,

name: scan0086-text-0174
text: Fig. 70.

name: scan0086-text-0175
text: High Tension Cable Carrying Plate

name: scan0086-text-0176
text: (showing the numbering).

name: scan0087-text-0178
text: Fig. 71.

name: scan0087-text-0179
text: Diagram indicating Sequence of Firing and

name: scan0087-text-0180
text: Distributor Connections.

name: scan0088-text-0182

name: scan0088-text-0184

name: scan0089-text-0186
text: TIMING AND CONTROL GEAR.

name: scan0089-text-0187
text: fitted with spring clip terminals to take ball knobs on

name: scan0089-text-0188
text: the plug electrodes. Carried by six steel clips or

name: scan0089-text-0189
text: brackets fixed under the heads of screws securing the

name: scan0089-text-0190
text: water pipe flanges to the induction manifolds, there is

name: scan0089-text-0191
text: a “U” shaped aluminium conduit tube with a large

name: scan0089-text-0192
text: opening at the base of the “U” by which the 24 leads

name: scan0089-text-0193
text: enter, and a series of small holes by which single leads

name: scan0089-text-0194
text: issue near their respective plugs. Between each distri-

name: scan0089-text-0195
