name: scan0118-text-0568
text: against the flange on the crankshaft nut; see that the

name: scan0118-text-0569
text: tongue of the locking wire engages both nuts properly.

name: scan0118-text-0570
text: See that the base chamber studs are tight. Be

name: scan0118-text-0571
text: careful not to injure the machined faces of the joint

name: scan0118-text-0572
text: between the two halves. Blow out all oil ducts.

name: scan0118-text-0573
text: N.B.—Reassembling notes are combined with the

name: scan0118-text-0574
text: sequence of operations, because the engine presents a

name: scan0118-text-0575
text: few small traps for the unwary mechanic.

name: scan0118-text-0576
text: 1. Place the upper half of the base chamber upside

name: scan0118-text-0577
text: down on the stand, and make sure that it is spotlessly

name: scan0118-text-0578
text: clean. Oil the bearings. Ascertain that the oil trap is

name: scan0118-text-0579
text: already fitted in the rear compartment (Fig. 87).

name: scan0118-text-0580
text: Fig. 87.

name: scan0118-text-0581
text: Upper Half of Crankcase (rear end), showing Oil Trap.

name: scan0119-text-0583
text: 2. Before placing the crankshaft in position, ascer-

name: scan0119-text-0584
text: tain that

name: scan0119-text-0585
text: (a) The main distribution gear wheel is

name: scan0119-text-0586
text: assembled with the tooth marked “O”

name: scan0119-text-0587
text: in line with the “O” on the crankshaft

name: scan0119-text-0588
text: pange.

name: scan0119-text-0589
text: (b) The washers (or “sleeves”) of the

name: scan0119-text-0590
text: thrust bearing are selected from “thick”

name: scan0119-text-0591
text: and “thin,” so that the end play in the

name: scan0119-text-0592
text: crankcase grooves does not exceed

name: scan0119-text-0593
text: .001 in. on assembly.

name: scan0119-text-0594
text: On placing the crankshaft in position, see that the

name: scan0119-text-0595
text: thrust seats in the base chamber without end play.

name: scan0119-text-0596
text: 3. Fit the connecting rods. It does not intrinsi-

name: scan0119-text-0597
text: cally matter on which side the forked rods are assembled,

name: scan0119-text-0598
text: provided, of course, they are all on the same side. In-

name: scan0119-text-0599
text: structions are that they shall be fitted on the right-hand

name: scan0119-text-0600
text: block. Each rod is stamped with a cylinder number

name: scan0119-text-0601
text: (1—6) on its web near the little end, the cylinders being

name: scan0119-text-0602
text: numbered from the rear of the engine, and not from the

name: scan0119-text-0603
text: propeller, as in British practice The numbered side of

name: scan0119-text-0604
text: each rod should be towards the rear of the engine. Oil

name: scan0119-text-0605
text: all bushes, and fill the crankpins and journals with oil.

name: scan0119-text-0606
text: N.B.—The split pins in the bolts of the forked rods

name: scan0119-text-0607
text: should be entered so that their heads are towards the

name: scan0119-text-0608
text: single rod; otherwise their bent ends will foul the

name: scan0119-text-0609
text: single rod.

name: scan0119-text-0610
text: 4. Place lower half of base chamber in position.

name: scan0119-text-0611
text: Do not insert any flange bolts, and tighten the nuts on

name: scan0119-text-0612
text: the front and rear bearing bolts only.

name: scan0119-text-0613
text: 5. Assemble the lower vertical shaft (pump drive)

name: scan0119-text-0614
text: with the deep-faced pinion at the cupped end of the

name: scan0119-text-0615
text: housing. Fit the shaft. and test the mesh of its upper

name: scan0119-text-0616
text: pinion with the crankshaft gear wheel. This should

name: scan0119-text-0617
text: be .007 in. cold, with limits of .005 in. and .010 in. If

name: scan0119-text-0618
text: the mesh is outside these limits pack shims (.002 in.

name: scan0119-text-0619
text: thick) between the crankshaft bevel and its flange until

name: scan0119-text-0620
text: the mesh is correct. Then tighten up the nuts on the

name: scan0119-text-0621
text: intermediate crankshaft bearing bolts. Invert the

name: scan0119-text-0622
text: assembly and fit all the bolts to the flanged joint of the

name: scan0119-text-0623
text: base chamber.

name: scan0119-text-0624
text: 6. Fit the pistons. Each piston is marked for

name: scan0119-text-0625
text: location (e.g., “R3”) and for weight in one of the

name: scan0119-text-0626
text: flats on its skirt. These marks should face the rear of

name: scan0119-text-0627
text: the engine. The weight marks indicate the number of

name: scan0119-text-0628
text: ounces by which a piston exceeds 3 lbs.; if a piston is

name: scan0119-text-0629
text: scrapped, the replacement should be of the original

name: scan0119-text-0630
text: weight to an ounce. Oil the gudgeon pins before inser-

name: scan0120-text-0632
text: tion. Replace the capping pieces, which should be a

name: scan0120-text-0633
text: light tapping fit.

name: scan0120-text-0634
text: 7. Each cylinder is numbered for location (e.g.,

name: scan0120-text-0635
text: “R3”) on the edge of its base flange near the water

name: scan0120-text-0636
text: inlet. Before fitting any cylinder, be sure that the

name: scan0120-text-0637
text: washer is in place on the base chamber studs; oil the

name: scan0120-text-0638
text: bore of the cylinder, and put the piston on the top of its

name: scan0120-text-0639
text: stroke. Push the cylinder down into place, and run

name: scan0120-text-0640
text: the holding-down nuts up with the fingers, but do not

name: scan0120-text-0641
text: tighten them. Fit the inlet port washers, and put the

name: scan0120-text-0642
text: induction manifolds in position, but delay replacing the

name: scan0120-text-0643
text: washers and nuts by which the manifolds are secured

name: scan0120-text-0644
text: to the cylinders. It is advisable to stop up the spark-

name: scan0120-text-0645
text: ing plug orifices at this point to prevent small parts from

name: scan0120-text-0646
text: being dropped into the combustion chambers.

name: scan0120-text-0647
text: 8. Next put a washer and nut on each of the studs

name: scan0120-text-0648
text: by which the manifolds are fixed to the cylinders. and

name: scan0120-text-0649
text: run the nuts up with the fingers. For tightening up the

name: scan0120-text-0650
text: cylinder, holding-down nuts and induction manifold nuts,

name: scan0120-text-0651
text: work by groups of three cylinders, and tighten each nut

name: scan0120-text-0652
text: a quarter of a turn in order, otherwise serious air leaks

name: scan0120-text-0653
text: at the inlet ports cannot be avoided.

name: scan0120-text-0654
text: 9. Soak the washers for the water joints between

name: scan0120-text-0655
text: the cylinders and the manifold jackets in water, and

name: scan0120-text-0656
text: refit them. Leave six of the screws at these joints loose

name: scan0120-text-0657
text: for the present (three down each side of the engine), as

name: scan0120-text-0658
text: they will be needed to fix the clips of the wiring U.

name: scan0120-text-0659
text: 10. Fit the front and rear water elbows with

name: scan0120-text-0660
text: washers beneath them. Before they are bolted down,

name: scan0120-text-0661
text: slip the coupling tube and its rubber connections into

name: scan0120-text-0662
text: place.

name: scan0120-text-0663
text: Fig. 88.

name: scan0120-text-0664
text: Housing and Bush of Lower Vertical Shaft.

name: scan0121-text-0002
text: 11. Insert the bolts by which the carburettors are

name: scan0121-text-0003
text: slung from the induction manifolds; fit the carburettors.

name: scan0121-text-0004
text: Particular care is required in refitting either type of

name: scan0121-text-0005
text: carburettor, owing to the general design of the induc-

name: scan0121-text-0006
text: tion assembly. Serious liability to air leaks exists at

name: scan0121-text-0007
text: four points, viz.:—

name: scan0121-text-0008
text: (a) Float chamber lids, where any appreciable

name: scan0121-text-0009
text: leak will reduce the range of the altitude

name: scan0121-text-0010
text: control.

name: scan0121-text-0011
text: (b) Joints between mixing and throttle

name: scan0121-text-0012
text: chambers.

name: scan0121-text-0013
text: (c) Joints between carburettor flanges and

name: scan0121-text-0014
text: ports in underside of induction manifolds.

name: scan0121-text-0015
text: (d) Joints between induction manifolds and

name: scan0121-text-0016
text: cylinder inlet ports.

name: scan0121-text-0017
text: On the Zenith carburettors a single paper washer

name: scan0121-text-0018
text: covered with gold size should be used to cover joints

name: scan0121-text-0019
text: (a) and (b); take great care to clean off old adhesive

name: scan0121-text-0020
text: before refitting, and cut holes in the washer large

name: scan0121-text-0021
text: enough to clear leak-holes and slow-running wells.

name: scan0121-text-0022
text: Tighten the nuts evenly and gradually.

name: scan0121-text-0023
text: Even greater care is required to insure tight joints

name: scan0121-text-0024
text: at the points (c) and (d), which form a supreme test of

name: scan0121-text-0025
text: first-class assembling. At (c) one unit (a carburettor)

name: scan0121-text-0026
text: beds up against two separate units (right and left mani-

name: scan0121-text-0027
text: folds); at (d) one unit (a manifold) beds against three

name: scan0121-text-0028
text: separate cylinders. A fragment of grit on any surface

name: scan0121-text-0029
text: concerned in such composite joints may lead to serious

name: scan0121-text-0030
text: air leaks. The joint at (c) is most satisfactorily made

name: scan0121-text-0031
text: from sheet “Hallite.”

name: scan0121-text-0032
text: Fig. 89.

name: scan0121-text-0033
text: Water Joint Clip.

name: scan0122-text-0035
text: IV.—VALVE TIMING INSTRUCTIONS.

name: scan0122-text-0036
text: Fit the carburettor controls and synchronise them.

name: scan0122-text-0037
text: 12. Time the valves.

name: scan0122-text-0038
text: The drawing on p. 123 and the data on this page

name: scan0122-text-0039
text: will probably provide all the information required by

name: scan0122-text-0040
text: skilled hands.

name: scan0122-text-0041
text: Full verbal instructions are, however, added as

name: scan0122-text-0042
text: follows:—

name: scan0122-text-0043
text: (i) Timing by the marks, p. 124.

name: scan0122-text-0044
text: (ii) Timing with a new camshaft or gear wheel,

name: scan0122-text-0046
text: (iii) Timing regardless of the marks (as, for in-

name: scan0122-text-0047
text: stance, when one of the units has been in-

name: scan0122-text-0048
text: accurately assembled), p. 127.

name: scan0122-text-0049
text: Note :—It will be observed that the exhaust closing

name: scan0122-text-0050
text: and inlet opening angles are identical; this point is

name: scan0122-text-0051
text: termed the “neutral point” in American instructional

name: scan0122-text-0052
text: matter. But the latest instructions from America give

name: scan0122-text-0053
text: the following alterations:—Exhaust valve opens 48°

name: scan0122-text-0054
text: before B.D.C.; closes 8° after T.D.C.; exhaust tappet

name: scan0122-text-0055
text: clearance, .019 in.

name: scan0122-text-0056
text: Firing order according to location of cylinders:

name: scan0122-text-0057
text: Firing order according to actual numbers on

name: scan0122-text-0058
text: cylinders:

name: scan0122-text-0060
text: Fig. 90.

name: scan0122-text-0061
text: Numbering of Cylinders.

name: scan0122-text-0062
text: (N.B.—The cylinders are numbered from the rear,

name: scan0122-text-0063
text: not from the propeller.)

name: scan0123-text-0093
text: Timing Marks.—The parts are clearly marked for

name: scan0123-text-0094
text: timing, but it must be understood that these marks are

name: scan0123-text-0095
text: only valid if the crankshaft and camshafts are correctly

name: scan0123-text-0096
text: assembled as units prior to fitting up the distribution

name: scan0123-text-0097
text: gears in the complete assembly. The three following

name: scan0123-text-0098
text: points are vital:—

name: scan0123-text-0099
text: (i) The main crankshaft bevel must be bolted

name: scan0123-text-0100
text: to its flange so that the tooth marked

name: scan0123-text-0101
text: marked “O” registers with the “O”

name: scan0123-text-0102
text: on the crankshaft flange.

name: scan0123-text-0103
text: (ii) The three zero marks stamped on the

name: scan0123-text-0104
text: camshaft, camshaft driven bevel, and dis-

name: scan0123-text-0105
text: tributor driving hub must be in line and

name: scan0123-text-0106
text: adjacent to each other.

name: scan0123-text-0107
text: (iii) The driving bevel of the long inclined

name: scan0123-text-0108
text: shaft has a tooth marked “O.” This

name: scan0123-text-0109
text: tooth must be set on the centre line of

name: scan0123-text-0110
text: the cylinder blocks, but towards the rear

name: scan0123-text-0111
text: of the engine—i.e., so that the three “O”

name: scan0123-text-0112
text: marks described in the last paragraph are

name: scan0123-text-0113
text: aligned down the centre of the cylinder

name: scan0123-text-0114
text: block beneath the camshaft centre.

name: scan0123-text-0115
text: If the above parts are assembled in the stated rela-

name: scan0123-text-0116
text: tions, the remaining timing marks insure correct timing

name: scan0123-text-0117
text: at the first attempt.

name: scan0123-text-0118
text: Fig. 91.

name: scan0123-text-0119
text: Timing Marks on Camshaft Flange and

name: scan0123-text-0120
text: Distributor Hub.

name: scan0124-text-0122
text: The rear face of the fixed flange of the propeller

name: scan0124-text-0123
text: hub is marked with the top dead centres of the three

name: scan0124-text-0124
text: crank throws, and also with marks at 10° after

name: scan0124-text-0125
text: each top dead centre—i.e., at the exhaust closing and

name: scan0124-text-0126
text: inlet opening angles (or “neutral points”). In lieu of

name: scan0124-text-0127
text: pointers, two dots are stamped on each side of the top

name: scan0124-text-0128
text: of the nose piece to indicate the centre line of each

name: scan0124-text-0129
text: cylinder block. (Exhaust valves now close at 8° after

name: scan0124-text-0130
text: T.D.C.)

name: scan0124-text-0131
text: The polished teeth found in some of the gears are

name: scan0124-text-0132
text: tool marks, not timing marks.

name: scan0124-text-0133
text: Timing Hints.—The following notes will not be re-

name: scan0124-text-0134
text: quired by experienced mechanic’s, but may be of assist-

name: scan0124-text-0135
text: ance to fitters accustomed only to vertical engines:—

name: scan0124-text-0136
text: (a) In timing a Vee engine, each camshaft

name: scan0124-text-0137
text: must be correctly timed in relation to the

name: scan0124-text-0138
text: other camshaft, as well as to the crank-

name: scan0124-text-0139
text: shaft.

name: scan0124-text-0140
text: (b) The timing marks are only valid if the

name: scan0124-text-0141
text: crankshaft is maintained in a certain posi-

name: scan0124-text-0142
text: tion, and this position is the same for

name: scan0124-text-0143
text: both cylinder blocks—i.e., after timing

name: scan0124-text-0144
text: the left-hand camshaft with the crank-

name: scan0124-text-0145
text: shaft at 10° past T.D.C., for that block,

name: scan0124-text-0146
text: Fig. 92.

name: scan0124-text-0147
text: Timing Marks on Propeller Hub Flange.

name: scan0126-text-0149
text: Fig. 93.

name: scan0126-text-0150
text: Distribution Gear in Section, explaining Timing Marks.

name: scan0126-text-0151
text: (N.B.—Crankshaft must be retained in above position

name: scan0126-text-0152
text: for timing both camshafts, when timing is done by

name: scan0126-text-0153
text: the marks.)

name: scan0127-text-0155
text: TIMING METHODS.

name: scan0127-text-0156
text: the crankshaft is not moved on 45° to

name: scan0127-text-0157
text: 10° past T.D.C. for timing the right-hand

name: scan0127-text-0158
text: camshaft.

name: scan0127-text-0159
text: (c) The operator will be standing so as to

name: scan0127-text-0160
text: face the rear or distribution gear end of

name: scan0127-text-0161
text: the engine during the job. Viewed from

name: scan0127-text-0162
text: this position, the crankshaft and cam-

name: scan0127-text-0163
text: shafts revolve clockwise.

name: scan0127-text-0164
text: Timing by the Marks.—See p. 126 for directions

name: scan0127-text-0165
text: when a new camshaft or camshaft gear have been

name: scan0127-text-0166
text: fitted. Otherwise, the order of procedure is as follows:—

name: scan0127-text-0167
text: 1. See that the “O” tooth on the crankshaft

name: scan0127-text-0168
text: bevel registers with the “O” on the crankshaft flange.

name: scan0127-text-0169
text: 2. Fit the vertical shaft, and insert its grubscrew.

name: scan0127-text-0170
text: This shaft acts as intermediate gearing; consequently

name: scan0127-text-0171
text: its teeth are not marked, and it does not matter in what

name: scan0127-text-0172
text: position it is inserted. Remember that it cannot be

name: scan0127-text-0173
text: fitted after the “idler” or short inclined shafts are in

name: scan0127-text-0174
text: place. Insert the grubscrew in the top flange of its

name: scan0127-text-0175
text: housing.

name: scan0127-text-0176
text: 3. Verify the backlash between the main driving

name: scan0127-text-0177
text: bevel and the driven bevel of the upper vertical shaft.

name: scan0127-text-0178
text: The backlash should measure .007 in. with the engine

name: scan0127-text-0179
text: cold. If it is incorrect, the shims between the crank-

name: scan0127-text-0180
text: shaft bevel and its flange must be reset.

name: scan0127-text-0181
text: 4. Set the crankshaft so that cranks Nos. 1 and 6

name: scan0127-text-0182
text: are 10° past the T.D.C. of the left-hand cylinder block,

name: scan0127-text-0183
text: viewing the engine from the rear. From this stand-

name: scan0127-text-0184
text: point, the crankshaft revolves clockwise, and the cranks

name: scan0127-text-0185
text: will therefore be 10° to the right of the axis of the left-

name: scan0127-text-0186
text: hand cylinder block, or 12

name: scan0127-text-0190
text: ° to the left of a vertical line

name: scan0127-text-0191
text: bisecting the Vee angle between the blocks.

name: scan0127-text-0192
text: N.B.—The crankshaft must not be moved until the

name: scan0127-text-0193
text: timing operations are complete, and remains in this

name: scan0127-text-0194
text: setting whilst the right-hand camshaft is assembled. If

name: scan0127-text-0195
text: the propeller hub is not in place, a depth gauge is very

name: scan0127-text-0196
text: convenient, as the sparking plug bosses are vertically

name: scan0127-text-0197
text: over the pistons.

name: scan0127-text-0198
text: 5. Fit the “idler” or short (lower) inclined shafts.

name: scan0127-text-0199
text: At the top of each shaft there are a pair of splines, set

name: scan0127-text-0200
text: at 180°, and marked by V nicks and red enamel. The

name: scan0127-text-0201
text: lines indicated by these opposed marks must run “fore

name: scan0127-text-0202
text: and aft”—i.e., parallel to the crankshaft axis; but it

name: scan0127-text-0203
text: does not matter in the least which of the two marked

name: scan0127-text-0204
text: teeth in each case is towards the front or rear of the

name: scan0127-text-0205
text: engine.

name: scan0129-text-0207
text: 6. Be sure that the “O” tooth of the small bevel

name: scan0129-text-0208
text: at the top end of the long inclined shaft is on the centre

name: scan0129-text-0209
text: line of the cylinder block, when it will, of course, be in

name: scan0129-text-0210
text: line with the “O” marks on the camshaft and large cam-

name: scan0129-text-0211
text: shaft bevel.

name: scan0129-text-0212
text: This will bring the marked splines at base of in-

name: scan0129-text-0213
text: clined shaft into the “fore and aft” position.

name: scan0129-text-0214
text: 8. Carefully retaining the camshaft and crankshaft

name: scan0129-text-0215
text: in these stipulated settings, lower the camshaft into

name: scan0129-text-0216
text: place, and mesh the splined joint between the upper

name: scan0129-text-0217
text: inclined shaft and the “idler” or short inclined shaft

name: scan0129-text-0218
text: with the marked splines in line.

name: scan0129-text-0219
text: Take care that no washers have been left threaded

name: scan0129-text-0220
text: on the camcase supporting studs, or the unit will have

name: scan0129-text-0221
text: to be dismantled again in order to bed the camcase

name: scan0129-text-0222
text: truly, and to obtain the correct valve clearances.

name: scan0129-text-0223
text: 9. Being careful not to disturb the settings of the

name: scan0129-text-0224
text: crankshaft and left-hand camshaft, fit the right-hand

name: scan0129-text-0225
text: camshaft unit into position on exactly the same system.

name: scan0129-text-0226
text: 10. When the assembly is completed, test and, if

name: scan0129-text-0227
text: necessary, adjust all tappet clearances, making the

name: scan0129-text-0228
text: tests with each cylinder on its fully retarded firing

name: scan0129-text-0229
text: point—i.e., at 10° past T.D.C. To find this point,

name: scan0129-text-0230
text: remember that the firing point (at full retard) of No. 1

name: scan0129-text-0231
text: Fig. 94.

name: scan0129-text-0232
text: Timing Marks on Camshafts and Inclined Shafts.

name: scan0130-text-0234
text: Timing with a New Camshaft or New Camshaft

name: scan0130-text-0235
text: Gear Wheel.

name: scan0130-text-0236
text: cylinder in either block is the “neutral point” of No. 6

name: scan0130-text-0237
text: cylinder on the same side, i.e., Nc. 6 piston is also at 10°

name: scan0130-text-0238
text: past T.D.C., its exhaust valve having just closed and its

name: scan0130-text-0239
text: inlet valve being at the opening point. These numbers go

name: scan0130-text-0240
text: by sevens, so that if No. 2 cylinder is at its firing point (full

name: scan0130-text-0241
text: retard), No. 5 on the same side is at the neutral point;

name: scan0130-text-0242
text: or if No. 3 is at the firing point, No. 4 is at the neutral

name: scan0130-text-0243
text: point. Thus, if the operator wishes to set the tappet

name: scan0130-text-0244
text: clearances of cylinder No. R6, he will turn the crank-

name: scan0130-text-0245
text: shaft and watch the exhaust valve of cylinder No. R1.

name: scan0130-text-0246
text: When No. R6 exhaust shuts, and just before No. R6 inlet

name: scan0130-text-0247
text: opens, cylinder No. R.1 must be on its firing point (fully

name: scan0130-text-0248
text: retarded)—i.e., correct for the setting of its clearances.

name: scan0130-text-0249
text: With a cold engine the exhaust tappet clearance should

name: scan0130-text-0250
text: be between .019 and .021 in., and the inlet tappet clearance

name: scan0130-text-0251
text: between .014 and .016 in. If the clearances are incorrect,

name: scan0130-text-0252
text: a combination of the thick, medium, and thin shims

name: scan0130-text-0253
text: threaded on the tappet (.015, .008, and .003 in. thick

name: scan0130-text-0254
text: respectively) will insure an accurate adjustment.

name: scan0130-text-0255
text: This may be done with the aid of the marks on

name: scan0130-text-0256
text: other parts as follows:—

name: scan0130-text-0257
text: (a) Leaving the camshaft gear unmounted, set

name: scan0130-text-0258
text: cranks Nos. 1—6 at 10° past T.D.C. for the left-hand

name: scan0130-text-0259
text: bock. Set the marked splines of the upper and lower

name: scan0130-text-0260
text: lower inclined shafts fore and aft. Set the marked tooth

name: scan0130-text-0261
text: on gear wheel of upper inclined shaft at the rear, and on

name: scan0130-text-0262
text: the centre line of the cylinder.

name: scan0130-text-0263
text: (b) Keeping the above settings, turn the left-hand

name: scan0130-text-0264
text: camshaft clockwise till No. L6 exhaust valve has just

name: scan0130-text-0265
text: closed, and No. L6 inlet is about to open.

name: scan0130-text-0266
text: (c) Mesh the camshaft gear wheel so that the

name: scan0130-text-0267
text: teeth and the flange bolt holes line up perfectly.

name: scan0130-text-0268
text: The camshaft gear wheel has 48 teeth, and is bolted

name: scan0130-text-0269
text: to its flange by seven bolts; this affords an adjustment

name: scan0130-text-0270
text: of one-seventh of a tooth space, or 2 1/7 degrees on the

name: scan0130-text-0271
text: crankshaft.

name: scan0130-text-0272
text: (d) Tighten up two of the bolts securing the cam-

name: scan0130-text-0273
text: shaft gear wheel, and check the tappet clearances in the

name: scan0130-text-0274
text: left-hand block.

name: scan0130-text-0275
text: (e) Test whether the exhausts close and the

name: scan0130-text-0276
text: inlets open at 10° past T.D.C. If they are late, move

name: scan0130-text-0277
text: the gear wheel clockwise one or more holes without dis-

name: scan0130-text-0278
text: turbing the setting of the camshaft or inclined shaft,

name: scan0130-text-0279
text: remembering that each advance of one bolt hole is equal

name: scan0131-text-0281
text: Timing Without Using the Marks.

name: scan0131-text-0282
text: to slightly more than 2° on the crank. If they are

name: scan0131-text-0283
text: early, move the gear wheel anti-clockwise in similar

name: scan0131-text-0284
text: fashion. (Exhausts are now set to close at 8° A.T.D.C.).

name: scan0131-text-0285
text: Always check the timing angles by turning the

name: scan0131-text-0286
text: engine in the direction of rotation to avoid slight in-

name: scan0131-text-0287
text: accuracies due to backlash in the gears.

name: scan0131-text-0288
text: When the camshaft gear wheel is correctly located

name: scan0131-text-0289
text: on the camshaft, set the distributor flange (marked

name: scan0131-text-0290
text: “L”) over the bolts, so that its marked notch is lined

name: scan0131-text-0291
text: up with the marked tooth on the pinion on the inclined

name: scan0131-text-0292
text: shaft.

name: scan0131-text-0293
text: Lastly, tighten up the bolts, and punch an “O”

name: scan0131-text-0294
text: on the gear wheel in line with the marked tooth on the

name: scan0131-text-0295
text: inclined shaft pinion; the assembly can in future be

name: scan0131-text-0296
text: timed by the marks.

name: scan0131-text-0297
text: To set the right-hand camshaft, turn the crank-

name: scan0131-text-0298
text: shaft till No. 1 crank is at 10° past T.D.C. in the right-

name: scan0131-text-0299
text: hand block. Then turn the camshaft till No. R1

name: scan0131-text-0300
text: exhaust has just shut, and No. R1 inlet is about to open.

name: scan0131-text-0301
text: Set the camshaft gear wheel as directed for the left-hand

name: scan0131-text-0302
text: shaft.

name: scan0131-text-0303
text: Before mounting the right-hand distributor flange,

name: scan0131-text-0304
text: turn the crankshaft backwards 45°, and set the distri-

name: scan0131-text-0305
text: butor driving flange so that its marked notch is lined

name: scan0131-text-0306
text: up with the marked tooth on the pinion at the top of the

name: scan0131-text-0307
text: inclined shaft, i.e., in the centre line of the right-hand

name: scan0131-text-0308
text: cylinder block. Bolt up and mark the gear wheel.

name: scan0131-text-0309
text: Circumstances may arise when, owing to mistakes

name: scan0131-text-0310
text: in assembly, it may be desirable to retime an engine

name: scan0131-text-0311
text: without reference to the marks. In this case, the

name: scan0131-text-0312
text: camshaft gear wheels may be unbolted, and the crank-

name: scan0131-text-0313
text: shaft set by the aid of the angles stamped on the pro-

name: scan0131-text-0314
text: peller hub; the procedure will be as follows:—

name: scan0131-text-0315
text: 1. Unbolt both camshaft gear wheels.

name: scan0131-text-0316
text: 2. Set the crankshaft at 10° past T.D.C. for

name: scan0131-text-0317
text: cylinder No. L1.

name: scan0131-text-0318
text: 3. Set the left-hand camshaft so that the inlet

name: scan0131-text-0319
text: valve of cylinder No. L6 is just about to

name: scan0131-text-0320
text: open, its exhaust valve having just shut.

name: scan0131-text-0321
text: 4. Replace the driven bevel of the left-hand cam-

name: scan0131-text-0322
text: shaft, and the distributor driving flange as

name: scan0131-text-0323
text: directed on page 121.

name: scan0131-text-0324
text: 5. Turn the crankshaft clockwise (as viewed from

name: scan0131-text-0325
text: the rear end) through 45°, when crank No. 6

name: scan0131-text-0326
text: will be at 10° past T.D.C. in R6 cylinder.

name: scan0132-text-0328
text: 6. Set the right-hand camshaft so that the inlet

name: scan0132-text-0329
text: valve of cylinder R1 is just about to open, its

name: scan0132-text-0330
text: exhaust valve having just shut.

name: scan0132-text-0331
text: 7. Replace the driven bevel of the right-hand cam-

name: scan0132-text-0332
text: shaft, and fit the distributor driving flange as

name: scan0132-text-0333
text: directed on page 86. (Experienced mechanics

name: scan0132-text-0334
text: will need no reminder that the crankshaft must

name: scan0132-text-0335
text: be turned through 45° only between timing

name: scan0132-text-0336
text: the two camshafts, and that whichever cylin-

name: scan0132-text-0337
text: der is selected as the basis of timing the left-

name: scan0132-text-0338
text: hand camshaft settles the cylinder to be em-

name: scan0132-text-0339
text: ployed in setting the right-hand camshaft, i.e.,

name: scan0132-text-0340
text: the selected cylinder of the right-hand block

name: scan0132-text-0341
text: must come next after the selected cylinder of

name: scan0132-text-0342
text: the left-hand block in the firing order.)

name: scan0132-text-0343
text: It is not possible, as might be supposed, to lift out

name: scan0132-text-0344
text: the vertical shaft, and to use this as an intermediate

name: scan0132-text-0345
text: gear in retiming operations, because its base fouls the

name: scan0132-text-0346
text: base of the idler shaft housings.

name: scan0132-text-0347
text: Obviously, the extended bolt holes in the rear end

name: scan0132-text-0348
text: plate of the camcases are not concerned with valve

name: scan0132-text-0349
text: timing, but are provided to assist in timing the ignition.

name: scan0132-text-0350
text: (Note: Exhaust now opens 48° B.B.D.C., and

name: scan0132-text-0351
text: closes 8° A.T.D.C.)

name: scan0132-text-0352
text: Fig. 95.

name: scan0132-text-0353
text: Timing Diagram.

name: scan0133-text-0355
text: Reassembling Notes (continued from p. 120.)

name: scan0133-text-0356
text: 13. Time the Ignition.—Full directions are given

name: scan0133-text-0357
text: on page 87.

name: scan0133-text-0358
text: 14. Connect up the sparking plug cables. Sparking

name: scan0133-text-0359
text: plugs on the propeller sides of the cylinders are

name: scan0133-text-0360
text: connected to the left-hand distributor; plugs

name: scan0133-text-0361
text: on the rear sides of the cylinders to the right-

name: scan0133-text-0362
text: hand distributors.

name: scan0133-text-0363
text: 15. Fit the water pump unit. Be careful not to

name: scan0133-text-0364
text: omit the jointing washer. Test the mesh of

name: scan0133-text-0365
text: the bevel gears (minimum backlash .005 in.,

name: scan0133-text-0366
text: maximum .010 in.). If the mesh is incorrect,

name: scan0133-text-0367
text: set it by placing shims between the jointing

name: scan0133-text-0368
text: washer and the pump casing.

name: scan0133-text-0369
text: 16. Fit the water inlet manifolds on either side of

name: scan0133-text-0370
text: the engine, together with the extensions

name: scan0133-text-0371
text: coupling them to the pump, and all necessary

name: scan0133-text-0372
text: rubber connections. See that the water clips

name: scan0133-text-0373
text: bear evenly on the hose, but do not tighten

name: scan0133-text-0374
text: them so as to bite into the rubber.

name: scan0133-text-0375
text: 17. Fit the oil pump unit. Make a sound joint with

name: scan0133-text-0376
text: a washer, but see that the washer clears the

name: scan0133-text-0377
text: oil leads both in the pump casing and in the

name: scan0133-text-0378
text: base chamber.

name: scan0133-text-0379
text: 18. Fit the base chamber breathers and the cover

name: scan0133-text-0380
text: of the front oil well.

name: scan0133-text-0381
text: Fig. 96.

name: scan0133-text-0382
text: Rear End of Crankcase from beneath, with

name: scan0133-text-0383
text: Oil Pump removed.

name: scan0134-text-0385
text: CHAPTER VII.

name: scan0134-text-0386
text: Possible Troubles.

name: scan0134-text-0387
text: I.—DIFFICULTY IN STARTING.

name: scan0134-text-0388
text: II.—LOSS OF POWER.

name: scan0134-text-0389
text: The following hints are arranged under four head-

name: scan0134-text-0390
text: ings, viz., difficulty in starting, loss of power, over-

name: scan0134-text-0391
text: heating, and lubrication.

name: scan0134-text-0392
text: (i) Weak mixture. Insufficient doping, or cylinders

name: scan0134-text-0393
text: not filled with mixture. Lack of petrol: examine tank,

name: scan0134-text-0394
text: tap, carburettor, and feed pipes.

name: scan0134-text-0395
text: (ii) Over-rich mixture; excessive doping or flood-

name: scan0134-text-0396
text: ing. (Rotate engine ten or twelve times backwards to

name: scan0134-text-0397
text: clear cylinders.)

name: scan0134-text-0398
text: (iii) Valves stuck or blowing.

name: scan0134-text-0399
text: (iv) Battery requires charging or attention to

name: scan0134-text-0400
text: acid. (See p. 92.)

name: scan0134-text-0401
text: (v) Faulty sparking plugs.

name: scan0134-text-0402
text: (vi) Faulty connections, e.g.—

name: scan0134-text-0403
text: (a) Loose terminals.

name: scan0134-text-0404
text: (b) Cables chafed or perished, producing short

name: scan0134-text-0405
text: circuits.

name: scan0134-text-0406
text: (c) Faulty switches.

name: scan0134-text-0407
text: (d) Mistakes in wiring.

name: scan0134-text-0408
text: (vii) Air leaks at joints of carburettors and induc-

name: scan0134-text-0409
text: tion manifolds.

name: scan0134-text-0410
text: (viii) Engine “gummy” with congealed oil.

name: scan0134-text-0411
text: (Note: In cold weather an engine which has not

name: scan0134-text-0412
text: been artificially heated will usually misfire for a short

name: scan0134-text-0413
text: period after first starting up.)

name: scan0134-text-0414
text: (i) Faulty sparking plugs, e.g.—

name: scan0134-text-0415
text: (a) Dirty.

name: scan0134-text-0416
text: (b) Excessive gap (the correct gap is .015 in.).

name: scan0134-text-0417
text: (c) Loose electrodes.

name: scan0134-text-0418
text: (d) Failure of insulation.

name: scan0135-text-0420
text: (ii) Defects in distributor “heads.” Test each

name: scan0135-text-0421
text: distributor head separately; it is improbable that both

name: scan0135-text-0422
text: will fail simultaneously, especially as each can function

name: scan0135-text-0423
text: with one of its contact breakers out of action. (See

name: scan0135-text-0425
text: (iii) Carburation, e.g.—

name: scan0135-text-0426
text: (a) Dirty filter.

name: scan0135-text-0427
text: (b) Insufficient pressure in tank.

name: scan0135-text-0428
text: (c) Feed pipe partly choked.

name: scan0135-text-0429
text: (d) Flooding, due to dirt on needle seating,

name: scan0135-text-0430
text: worn needle, toggle, levers sticking, or a

name: scan0135-text-0431
text: punctured float.

name: scan0135-text-0432
text: (e) Dirt in the jets.

name: scan0135-text-0433
text: (f) Water in the carburettor.

name: scan0135-text-0434
text: (g) Serious air leaks at the cylinder to mani-

name: scan0135-text-0435
text: fold or manifold to carburettor joints.

name: scan0135-text-0436
text: (h) Altitude control accidentally set open.

name: scan0135-text-0437
text: (iv) Overheating. Many of the troubles listed

name: scan0135-text-0438
text: under III., below, will produce loss of power, accom-

name: scan0135-text-0439
text: panied by misfiring, during their earlier phases.

name: scan0135-text-0440
text: (v) Valves.

name: scan0135-text-0441
text: (a) One or more valves stuck up through dirt,

name: scan0135-text-0442
text: overheating, etc.

name: scan0135-text-0443
text: (b) Carbon on valve seating.

name: scan0135-text-0444
text: (c) Broken valve springs.

name: scan0135-text-0445
text: (d) Valve warped.

name: scan0135-text-0446
text: (e) Serious wear of valve guides, resulting in

name: scan0135-text-0447
text: air leaks.

name: scan0135-text-0448
text: (f) Tappets out of adjustment.

name: scan0135-text-0449
text: (vi) Piston rings broken or “baked” into grooves.

name: scan0135-text-0450
text: (vii) Valves.

name: scan0135-text-0451
text: (a) Incorrect valve clearances (the correct

name: scan0135-text-0452
text: clearances are .015 in. for the inlets, and

name: scan0135-text-0453
text: .019 in. for the exhausts).

name: scan0135-text-0454
text: (b) Weak valve springs; a weight of 45 lbs.

name: scan0135-text-0455
text: is required to compress an outer

name: scan0135-text-0456
text: exhaust spring to 2

name: scan0135-text-0460
text: in., and 23

name: scan0135-text-0464
text: lbs. for

name: scan0135-text-0465
text: an outer inlet valve spring.

name: scan0135-text-0466
text: (c) Valves wrongly timed. Inlet opens 10°

name: scan0135-text-0467
text: after T.D.C., closes 45° after B.D.C. Ex-

name: scan0135-text-0468
text: haust opens 50° (48°) before B.D.C.,

name: scan0135-text-0469
text: closes 10° (8°) after T.D.C.

name: scan0135-text-0470
text: (viii) Compression faults.

name: scan0135-text-0471
text: (a) Valves sticking, pitted, or warped.

name: scan0135-text-0472
text: (b) Leaks at the sparking plugs.

name: scan0135-text-0473
text: (c) Faulty piston rings. (Note:—All aluminium

name: scan0135-text-0474
text: pistons are necessarily given considerable

name: scan0136-text-0476
text: III.—OVERHEATING.

name: scan0136-text-0477
text: IV.—LUBRICATION TROUBLES.

name: scan0136-text-0478
text: clearance in the cylinders. If the piston

name: scan0136-text-0479
text: rings are worn, or inclined to stick in

name: scan0136-text-0480
text: their grooves, the compressicn will inevit-

name: scan0136-text-0481
text: ably be poor, but may improve as the

name: scan0136-text-0482
text: pistons grow hot and expand. When the

name: scan0136-text-0483
text: compression leaks past the piston, a dope

name: scan0136-text-0484
text: of lubricating oil, or of oil mixed with

name: scan0136-text-0485
text: paraffin, may be employed.)

name: scan0136-text-0486
text: (iii) Incorrect jets: the standard sizes for the

name: scan0136-text-0487
text: Liberty engines are:—

name: scan0136-text-0488
text: Zenith:—Main, 280 cc.; compensator, 340 cc.

name: scan0136-text-0489
text: Claudel:—Main jet, 490 c.c.; slow-running jet,

name: scan0136-text-0491
text: (i) Water circulation troubles.

name: scan0136-text-0492
text: (a) Lack of water; tank not full; radiator or

name: scan0136-text-0493
text: connections leaking.

name: scan0136-text-0494
text: (b) Impeller of pump sheared.

name: scan0136-text-0495
text: (c) Air lock; tail should be raised during re-

name: scan0136-text-0496
text: plenishment.

name: scan0136-text-0497
text: (d) Pipes partly blocked by dirt, fur, or ill-

name: scan0136-text-0498
text: made rubber connections.

name: scan0136-text-0499
text: (ii) Other causes.

name: scan0136-text-0500
text: (a) Overheated sparking plugs.

name: scan0136-text-0501
text: (b) Engine carbonised and in need of cleaning.

name: scan0136-text-0502
text: (c) Ignition accidentally retarded, or perhaps

name: scan0136-text-0503
text: mistimed.

name: scan0136-text-0504
text: (d) Weak mixture; altitude control partly

name: scan0136-text-0505
text: open, or serious air leaks at induction

name: scan0136-text-0506
text: manifold joints.

name: scan0136-text-0507
text: (e) Lubrication defective.

name: scan0136-text-0508
text: (i) Gauge registers over 55 lbs. Relief valve is de-

name: scan0136-text-0509
text: ranged. Stop engine and repair fault, or some pipe or

name: scan0136-text-0510
text: joint may burst.

name: scan0136-text-0511
text: (ii) Gauge registers little or no pressure. Leak

name: scan0136-text-0512
text: between gauge and pump. Pressure pump out of action,

name: scan0136-text-0513
text: gauge out of order.

name: scan0136-text-0514
text: Switch off and investigate.

name: scan0136-text-0515
text: The oil pressure varies with the engine revolutions,

name: scan0136-text-0516
text: and will always be low when the engine is only “ticking”

name: scan0136-text-0517
text: over.

name: scan0137-text-0519
text: CHAPTER VIII.

name: scan0137-text-0520
text: Installation of “Liberty”

name: scan0137-text-0521
text: Engine.

name: scan0137-text-0522
text: ENGINE MOUNTING.

name: scan0137-text-0523
text: ACCESSIBILITY OF ENGINE AND AUXILIARY

name: scan0137-text-0524
text: FITTINGS.

name: scan0137-text-0525
text: ENGINE CONTROLS.

name: scan0137-text-0526
text: A drawing showing the principal over-all engine

name: scan0137-text-0527
text: dimensions, and the dimensions of fixing centres is given

name: scan0137-text-0528
text: in the appendix. The engine mounting should be of fire-

name: scan0137-text-0529
text: proof construction, so far as possible. Air intake pipes

name: scan0137-text-0530
text: are to be arranged to come clear of the cowling, and the

name: scan0137-text-0531
text: necessary drains provided, so that any overflow petrol

name: scan0137-text-0532
text: may be discharged free of the fuselage.

name: scan0137-text-0533
text: Care is to be taken in mounting the engine in the

name: scan0137-text-0534
text: machine that facility is afforded for ready inspection of

name: scan0137-text-0535
text: all parts requiring attention. By designing the cowling

name: scan0137-text-0536
text: in a sufficient number of sections, or by the provision

name: scan0137-text-0537
text: of suitable hinged inspection doors, access must be

name: scan0137-text-0538
text: possible to the following parts:—

name: scan0137-text-0539
text: (1) Distributors, generator, and battery box.

name: scan0137-text-0540
text: (The distance from the after face of a distributor housing

name: scan0137-text-0541
text: and the forward face of any bulkhead aft of it must nct

name: scan0137-text-0542
text: be less than 10 in.)

name: scan0137-text-0543
text: (2) Sump inspection covers fore and aft, filters,

name: scan0137-text-0544
text: and oil pumps.

name: scan0137-text-0545
text: (3) Carburettors. It must be possible to remove

name: scan0137-text-0546
text: carburettors from the engine as entire units.

name: scan0137-text-0547
text: (4) Water pump.

name: scan0137-text-0548
text: (5) C.C. gun gear generator.

name: scan0137-text-0549
text: Positive type engine controls only must be fitted.

name: scan0137-text-0550
text: For example, the controls may be a combination of

name: scan0137-text-0551
text: push-and-pull rods, levers, bellcranks, and torsional

name: scan0137-text-0552
text: tubes. Essential engine controls comprise throttle,

name: scan0137-text-0553
text: altitude compensator, ignition and multiple-type petrol

name: scan0137-text-0554
text: cock; the precise design of the latter will naturally

name: scan0137-text-0555
text: depend on the type of petrol system. Subsidiary engine

name: scan0137-text-0556
text: controls must comprise temperature regulator for water

name: scan0137-text-0557
text: cooling system, an oil temperature regulator, and an

name: scan0137-text-0558
text: equalising cock, the latter being required between the

name: scan0137-text-0559
text: main petrol tanks of a dual petrol system. (See also

name: scan0137-text-0560
text: “Cooling System,” “Lubrication System,” and

name: scan0138-text-0562
text: PETROL SYSTEM.

name: scan0138-text-0563
text: “Petrol System.”) Guides are to be provided for all

name: scan0138-text-0564
text: rods over three feet in length; joints or attachments

name: scan0138-text-0565
text: of any kind are to be positively secured by pinning,

name: scan0138-text-0566
text: brazing, or hard soldering, and where torsion tubes are

name: scan0138-text-0567
text: used, care is to be taken that these are of sufficient

name: scan0138-text-0568
text: strength to avoid risk of permanent distortion.

name: scan0138-text-0569
text: An air pressure system of petrol feed is not recom-

name: scan0138-text-0570
text: mended. The system of fuel feed to be installed is

name: scan0138-text-0571
text: that in which a head corresponding to a pressure of

name: scan0138-text-0572
text: 2 lb. per sq. in. is derived from a small gravity tank,

name: scan0138-text-0573
text: or its equivalent, which is replenished as required by a

name: scan0138-text-0574
text: suitable form of petrol pump. If M.I.D. self-sealing

name: scan0138-text-0575
text: tanks have been specified, care is to be taken that

name: scan0138-text-0576
text: these are installed complete with filler caps, outlet

name: scan0138-text-0577
text: unions, and the like, and that no fittings are used other

name: scan0138-text-0578
text: than those incorporated in the design, and supplied

name: scan0138-text-0579
text: with the tanks. Where self-sealing tanks are not

name: scan0138-text-0580
text: installed, the dangers resulting from puncturing may

name: scan0138-text-0581
text: be lessened by dividing the main petrol tank into two

name: scan0138-text-0582
text: equal compartments. All tanks must be tested to

name: scan0138-text-0583
text: specification tank test, and care is to be taken in fixing,

name: scan0138-text-0584
text: that the weight of them is evenly distributed on the

name: scan0138-text-0585
text: upper and lower longerons in order to avoid undue

name: scan0138-text-0586
text: stressing. Ample packing of felt is to be placed between

name: scan0138-text-0587
text: the tank and bearers, and the practice of fitting up fixing

name: scan0138-text-0588
text: bolts with over-size washers and rubber packing is

name: scan0138-text-0589
text: advised. Except where specified to the contrary, as

name: scan0138-text-0590
text: above, fillers caps and seatings must be of A.G.S. design

name: scan0138-text-0591
text: and specification, and the former should be stamped

name: scan0138-text-0592
text: with the capacity and nature of the contents of the tank,

name: scan0138-text-0593
text: and be secured to the seating by a lanyard or guard

name: scan0138-text-0594
text: chain. The filler caps of all tanks not under air pressure

name: scan0138-text-0595
text: must be provided with a vent hole of not less than

name: scan0138-text-0599
text: in.

name: scan0138-text-0600
text: diameter. Filler tubes are to be fitted with a removable

name: scan0138-text-0601
text: gauze filter of Air Board standard. If the main petrol

name: scan0138-text-0602
text: tank be divided into two compartments, the petrol supply

name: scan0138-text-0603
text: pipes must be entirely independent of one another, and

name: scan0138-text-0604
text: a multiple or rotary cock comprising a distributing box

name: scan0138-text-0605
text: must be provided to enable the carburettors to be

name: scan0138-text-0606
text: supplied from any of the tanks at will. To enable the

name: scan0138-text-0607
text: contents of dual main tanks to be levelled, there is to be

name: scan0138-text-0608
text: fitted between the tanks a communicating U tube, the

name: scan0138-text-0609
text: latter connecting to unions in the bottom of the tanks

name: scan0138-text-0610
text: and fitted with an equalising cock operated from the

name: scan0138-text-0611
text: cockpit by a suitable control. In running pipes, sharp

name: scan0138-text-0612
text: bends, traps, and proximity to distributors must be

name: scan0138-text-0613
text: avoided. Protection against gunfire should be sought by

name: scan0139-text-0615
text: LUBRICATION SYSTEM.

name: scan0139-text-0616
text: running pipes behind the longerons, and, in a dual

name: scan0139-text-0617
text: system, by running the duplicated pipe lines on opposite

name: scan0139-text-0618
text: sides of the fuselage. All pipes must be thoroughly

name: scan0139-text-0619
text: cleaned before assembling. See that ample support is

name: scan0139-text-0620
text: provided by frequent felt-lined clips or saddles secured

name: scan0139-text-0621
text: to suitable parts of the machine. The area of the main

name: scan0139-text-0622
text: petrol pipe must be such that the flow of fuel sufficient

name: scan0139-text-0623
text: for maintaining full power is exceeded by 100 per cent.

name: scan0139-text-0624
text: when the carburettor unions are uncoupled and the

name: scan0139-text-0625
text: supply is in a condition of minimum head. The sizes of

name: scan0139-text-0626
text: the branch supply pipes to carburettors must be suit-

name: scan0139-text-0627
text: able for the unions provided on the carburettors.

name: scan0139-text-0628
text: Nipples, unions, and cocks are to be secured by hard

name: scan0139-text-0629
text: soldering. In the main petrol supply line to carburettors

name: scan0139-text-0630
text: there is to be provided a filter chamber fitted with gauze

name: scan0139-text-0631
text: of Air Board standard mesh, the latter accessible for

name: scan0139-text-0632
text: removal and cleaning. See that the joining of branch

name: scan0139-text-0633
text: pipes is made only with one-piece Y or T pieces.

name: scan0139-text-0634
text: Flexible connections of approved form are to be

name: scan0139-text-0635
text: provided near to all joints and unions, and petrol pipes

name: scan0139-text-0636
text: must be marked with a red band painted round them at

name: scan0139-text-0637
text: all places of connection. Possible flooding and over-

name: scan0139-text-0638
text: flowing from carburettors and air intakes is to be dis-

name: scan0139-text-0639
text: posed of free of the fuselage through drain pipes

name: scan0139-text-0640
text: arranged to operate irrespective of the position of flight.

name: scan0139-text-0641
text: The oil tank must have a capacity 20 per

name: scan0139-text-0642
text: cent. larger than the amount of oil required by the engine

name: scan0139-text-0643
text: for the flight endurance provided by the petrol tanks,

name: scan0139-text-0644
text: and must be situated so that there is a minimum head

name: scan0139-text-0645
text: of 4 in. over the inlet nipple of the oil pump. The in-

name: scan0139-text-0646
text: structions regarding petrol tank filler caps and the

name: scan0139-text-0647
text: running and jointing of petrol pipes apply also to oil

name: scan0139-text-0648
text: pipes. The pipes connecting the oil tank to the engine

name: scan0139-text-0649
text: must not be less than 1

name: scan0139-text-0653
text: in. O.D., and enlarging nipples

name: scan0139-text-0654
text: will accordingly be substituted on the pump fcr those

name: scan0139-text-0655
text: with which the engines are at present being delivered

name: scan0139-text-0656
text: from America. See that all oil pipes are marked with a

name: scan0139-text-0657
text: black band near to unions and on each side of all flexible

name: scan0139-text-0658
text: joints. The oil pressure gauge is to be fitted in such

name: scan0139-text-0659
text: a position that it can readily be seen by the pilot, and

name: scan0139-text-0660
text: is to be connected up with piping of the same size as

name: scan0139-text-0661
text: the union on the engine or the gauge. If an oil cock is

name: scan0139-text-0662
text: fitted between the tank and the oil pump, provision is

name: scan0139-text-0663
text: to be made for locking or sealing it in the open position.

name: scan0139-text-0664
text: A large diameter cock or drain plug is to be fitted in

name: scan0140-text-0666
text: COOLING SYSTEM.

name: scan0140-text-0667
text: the lowest part of the lubrication system for drainage

name: scan0140-text-0668
text: purposes. It is desirable that arrangements be made

name: scan0140-text-0669
text: in the oil tank for cooling the heated oil returned by the

name: scan0140-text-0670
text: scavenger pumps, and means of temperature regulation

name: scan0140-text-0671
text: must be provided.

name: scan0140-text-0672
text: Whatever position is adopted for the radiator, care

name: scan0140-text-0673
text: is to be taken that the load is so distributed that neither

name: scan0140-text-0674
text: the radiator nor supporting members are unevenly

name: scan0140-text-0675
text: stressed. The type of radiator proposed to be fitted

name: scan0140-text-0676
text: must in all cases be approved by the Controller, Techni-

name: scan0140-text-0677
text: cal Department. The water system is to be so

name: scan0140-text-0678
text: arranged that no air or steam locks can form. A head

name: scan0140-text-0679
text: of not less than 2 in. must remain above the outlet of

name: scan0140-text-0680
text: each cylinder when all reserve water has boiled or leaked

name: scan0140-text-0681
text: away, and when the machine is climbing at 25° to the

name: scan0140-text-0682
text: horizontal, gliding at 15°, or has a 10° list to either side.

name: scan0140-text-0683
text: Under normal conditions, reserve water must be allowed

name: scan0140-text-0684
text: for according to the following formula:—

name: scan0140-text-0685
text: The reserve water must be carried at the highest

name: scan0140-text-0686
text: point of the system, and a suitable header tank must

name: scan0140-text-0687
text: either be incorporated in the radiator or arranged for

name: scan0140-text-0688
text: separately. All connecting pipes must be of full bore to

name: scan0140-text-0689
text: suit the pump and engine top water pipe connections.

name: scan0140-text-0690
text: Care should be taken that outlet pipes from the engine

name: scan0140-text-0691
text: do not fall, and that reverse bends are avoided in all

name: scan0140-text-0692
text: water pipe work. Flexible connections of approved type

name: scan0140-text-0693
text: are to be provided near to all unions and brazed joints,

name: scan0140-text-0694
text: and the pipe lengths on each side of all connections are

name: scan0140-text-0695
text: to be marked with blue bands. The cooling system

name: scan0140-text-0696
text: must be arranged so that it may be completely drained.

name: scan0140-text-0697
text: The cocks must be of approved design and provided with

name: scan0140-text-0698
text: means of lccking them in closed position. Means are

name: scan0140-text-0699
text: to be provided for restricting at will the cooling surface

name: scan0140-text-0700
text: of the radiator.

name: scan0140-text-0701
text: A standard fitting for a distant reading thermome-

name: scan0140-text-0702
text: ter must be provided in the cooling system in such a

name: scan0140-text-0703
text: position that the temperature of the water leaving the

name: scan0140-text-0704
text: water jackets is registered. Where the radiator is near

name: scan0140-text-0705
text: to the engine, the thermometer bulb should be fixed in

name: scan0140-text-0706
text: the top header of the radiator as near as possible to and

name: scan0140-text-0707
text: parallel to the tube block, and vertically below the inlet

name: scan0140-text-0708
text: pipe.

name: scan0140-text-0709
text: When

name: scan0140-text-0710
text: N = Normal engine B.H.P.,

name: scan0140-text-0711
text: and

name: scan0140-text-0712
text: H = Hours’ fuel capacity allowed,

name: scan0140-text-0713
text: C = Reserve water required (gallons).

name: scan0140-text-0714
text: Then C = 1 +

name: scan0140-text-0715
text: H.N.

name: scan0141-text-0002
text: COWLING.

name: scan0141-text-0003
text: EXHAUST PIPES.

name: scan0141-text-0004
text: WIRING SYSTEM.

name: scan0141-text-0005
text: Care is to be taken that the small thermometer tube

name: scan0141-text-0006
text: leading back to the instrument board is well supported

name: scan0141-text-0007
text: by suitable clips and properly protected. On no account

name: scan0141-text-0008
text: should capillary tubes be cut off; these are supplied

name: scan0141-text-0009
text: in standard lengths, and, if too long, must be coiled up.

name: scan0141-text-0010
text: The cowling should be so designed that it affords

name: scan0141-text-0011
text: sufficient protection to the engine, and particularly that

name: scan0141-text-0012
text: it may protect from rain the distributor heads, sparking

name: scan0141-text-0013
text: plugs, and other electrical fittings. Inlet and outlet

name: scan0141-text-0014
text: louvres must be made for adequate air circulation over

name: scan0141-text-0015
text: the cylinder heads, and in the case of nose-piece radia-

name: scan0141-text-0016
text: tors, air outlets must also be provided for egress of air

name: scan0141-text-0017
text: entering through the radiator. Framework for support-

name: scan0141-text-0018
text: ing the engine cowling must be provided, and aluminium

name: scan0141-text-0019
text: of inverted channel section has been found suitable.

name: scan0141-text-0020
text: Unless special sanction of a different arrangement has

name: scan0141-text-0021
text: been granted, this framework must be bolted to the

name: scan0141-text-0022
text: fuselage itself, and on no account is it to be stayed or

name: scan0141-text-0023
text: attached to any part of the engine. The question of

name: scan0141-text-0024
text: accessibility of certain parts of the engine is to be borne

name: scan0141-text-0025
text: in mind in designing the cowling (see “Accessibility”

name: scan0141-text-0026
text: page 133), and the joining together of adjacent sections

name: scan0141-text-0027
text: by means of removable hinge pins is to be adopted.

name: scan0141-text-0028
text: A standard exhaust pipe has been designed for the

name: scan0141-text-0029
text: engine, and no other is to be fitted without special per-

name: scan0141-text-0030
text: mission from the Controller, Technical Department.

name: scan0141-text-0031
text: Modification of the exhaust extension pipe will be re-

name: scan0141-text-0032
text: quired in different machines, and attention must be given

name: scan0141-text-0033
text: to the direction in which the exhaust is discharged; the

name: scan0141-text-0034
text: pipes must not deliver on to the crew or to any part of

name: scan0141-text-0035
text: the aeroplane.

name: scan0141-text-0036
text: The wiring and switch system must be that incor-

name: scan0141-text-0037
text: porated in the engine design, and described in Chapter

name: scan0141-text-0038
text: IV. The special switch board and ammeter supplied

name: scan0141-text-0039
text: with the engine should be fitted up so that the ammeter

name: scan0141-text-0040
text: is easily readable by the pilot. A diagram of wiring is

name: scan0141-text-0041
text: shown in Fig. 73. All wires must run in continuous

name: scan0141-text-0042
text: lengths from terminal to terminal; cable ends should be

name: scan0141-text-0043
text: of approved type; and protection and support must be

name: scan0141-text-0044
text: provided for all wires.

name: scan0141-text-0045
text: Particular care is to be taken that the main leads

name: scan0141-text-0046
text: are of ample size, as under certain conditions currents

name: scan0142-text-0048
text: CHAPTER IX.

name: scan0142-text-0049
text: C. C. Synchronizing Gear on

name: scan0142-text-0050
text: Liberty Engine.

name: scan0142-text-0051
text: up to 20 amperes are required to be carried. Cables

name: scan0142-text-0052
text: should accordingly be 110/36 or area equivalent. The

name: scan0142-text-0053
text: battery box, which should be of spruce, varnished on the

name: scan0142-text-0054
text: outside, and thoroughly painted internally with anti-

name: scan0142-text-0055
text: sulphuric enamel, must be provided with packing slides.

name: scan0142-text-0056
text: An approved system of labelling all wires is to be

name: scan0142-text-0057
text: adopted, so that leads may be identified beyond possi-

name: scan0142-text-0058
text: bility of doubt. After installation all wiring is to be

name: scan0142-text-0059
text: tested out with bell and battery.

name: scan0142-text-0060
text: A special handbook dealing with the installation of

name: scan0142-text-0061
text: the Liberty engine in ‘De H. 9a aeroplanes is available

name: scan0142-text-0062
text: for issue.

name: scan0142-text-0063
text: At the rear end of the engine, concentric with the

name: scan0142-text-0064
text: crankshaft, there is a cover plate fitted with a register.

name: scan0142-text-0065
text: A cam box, with a splined shaft to engage in the hollow

name: scan0142-text-0066
text: end of the crankshaft, is provided with the engine, and

name: scan0142-text-0067
text: can be fitted in place of this cover. This box contains a

name: scan0142-text-0068
text: camshaft with a “single row” ball bearing, and the

name: scan0142-text-0069
text: Fig. 97.

name: scan0142-text-0070
text: C.C. Gun Gear.

name: scan0143-text-0072
text: shaft relies for its other support on the fit in the crank-

name: scan0143-text-0073
text: shaft. On the camshaft are mounted, first, a fixed

name: scan0143-text-0074
text: flange having serrations cut on one side; then two

name: scan0143-text-0075
text: double humped cams freely mounted, but having similar

name: scan0143-text-0076
text: serrations on their side, so that the serrations of the

name: scan0143-text-0077
text: first cam engage with those on the flange, and those on

name: scan0143-text-0078
text: the second cam engage with those on the first, the two

name: scan0143-text-0079
text: cams being held up by a central nut on the camshaft.

name: scan0143-text-0080
text: In line with the respective cams are two holes, hori-

name: scan0143-text-0081
text: zontally opposed, into which the cylinders are screwed.

name: scan0143-text-0082
text: These holes on the first engines are tapped 1 in. × 18 T,

name: scan0143-text-0083
text: right hand, and a cylinder with a special thread on one

name: scan0143-text-0084
text: end to fit this, has been got out. The holes in the

name: scan0143-text-0085
text: cam box are fitted with plugs when delivered; in the

name: scan0143-text-0086
text: case of machines being fitted with only one synchronized

name: scan0143-text-0087
text: gun, only one plug should be removed, and only one

name: scan0143-text-0088
text: cylinder and plunger will be required. These special

name: scan0143-text-0089
text: cylinders must be fitted until generators (or cam boxes)

name: scan0143-text-0090
text: are supplied tapped

name: scan0143-text-0094
text: in. B.S.P., which will enable the

name: scan0143-text-0095
text: standard B type cylinder to be used. Timing is effected

name: scan0143-text-0096
text: by slacking the nut and freeing the cam from the serra-

name: scan0143-text-0097
text: tions when the cam can be turned to the required

name: scan0143-text-0098
text: position.

name: scan0143-text-0099
text: The parts of standard gear required will be the B

name: scan0143-text-0100
text: type pipe lines, reservoir, etc., and B or C trigger

name: scan0143-text-0101
text: motors. A standard B type plunger for generator and

name: scan0143-text-0102
text: the special cylinder are also required; the rest of the

name: scan0143-text-0103
text: generator—including lubricatcr—is formed by the attach-

name: scan0143-text-0104
text: attachment herein described.

name: scan0143-text-0105
text: NOTE.—It is possible that the engines will be de-

name: scan0143-text-0106
text: livered with the generator already fitted instead of the

name: scan0143-text-0107
text: plate.

name: scan0143-text-0108
text: The synchronizing gear will only be required on

name: scan0143-text-0109
text: single engine tractor machines fitted with Vickers guns,

name: scan0143-text-0110
text: and in most cases it is probable that one cylinder and

name: scan0143-text-0111
text: plunger only will be required.

name: scan0146-text-0275
text: ADJUSTING CONTROLS OF ZENITH

name: scan0146-text-0276
text: CARBURETTOR.

name: scan0146-text-0277
text: Each duplex carburettor is fitted with two butterfly

name: scan0146-text-0278
text: throttle valves, and it may occasionally be found that

name: scan0146-text-0279
text: the pair are not accurately synchronised (see dotted

name: scan0146-text-0280
text: throttle positions shown in Fig. 98). No adjustment is

name: scan0146-text-0281
text: provided, and in such cases the butterfly must be very

name: scan0146-text-0282
text: carefully “set” so that the closing points agree.

name: scan0146-text-0283
text: It is further necessary to synchronise the throttles

name: scan0146-text-0284
text: of the fore and aft carburettors in coupling up the con-

name: scan0146-text-0285
text: necting rod, and this should be done as closely as is

name: scan0146-text-0286
text: compatible with taking up the backlash and torque in

name: scan0146-text-0287
text: the connecting rod. This is done by means of the screw

name: scan0146-text-0288
text: adjustment “X” in Fig. 99. If it is impossible to syn-

name: scan0146-text-0289
text: chronise both carburettors, and also to set the connecting

name: scan0146-text-0290
text: rod perfectly by one and the same adjustment, a slight

name: scan0146-text-0291
text: variation in the throttle closing points is preferable to a

name: scan0146-text-0292
text: sloppy setting of the rod. In this case the throttles of

name: scan0146-text-0293
text: the front carburettor should close very slightly in ad-

name: scan0146-text-0294
text: vance of the rear throttles.

name: scan0146-text-0295
text: Finally. the throttle stop screws (“Z” in Fig. 99)

name: scan0146-text-0296
text: must be set so that they relieve the butterfly valve of

name: scan0146-text-0297
text: excessive pressure when the control lever is slammed

name: scan0146-text-0298
text: back.
